description: Simple SummaryUnderstanding how colorectal tumours interact with immune cells is critical for improving immunotherapy responses. In this study, we used air–liquid interface organoids derived from patient tumours and adjacent healthy colon tissues to reproduce the original tumour microenvironment in the laboratory.

title: Dual calcium-voltage optical mapping of regional voltage and calcium signals in intact murine RyR2-R2474S hearts

description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). title: Building Research Capacity in Medical Radiation Sciences Through University–Clinical Partnerships: A Commentary on Working Smarter, Not Harder
creator: Therese Gunn, Michael Neep, Pamela Rowntree, Deborah Starkey
description: A research partnership model frames university–clinical collaboration as central to strengthening medical radiation sciences research capacity. By aligning students, academics, clinicians, resources, ethics processes, skills development and outputs, the model supports sustainable, evidence‐informed practice with potential benefits for patients and professionals. ‘I am neither especially clever nor especially gifted. I am only very, very curious.

title: Current Knowledge on UTUC Epidemiology in Poland Compared to Europe
creator: Iwona Wnętrzak, Urszula Wojciechowska, Jakub Dobruch, Mateusz Czajkowski, Roman Sosnowski, Wojciech Krajewski, Marcin Matuszewski, Piotr Marczyński, Joanna A. Didkowska
description: Simple SummaryUpper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) is a rare cancer with limited epidemiological data from Central and Eastern Europe. Using nationwide Polish and European data from two decades, we analyzed UTUC incidence, mortality, and survival patterns. Poland shows a distinct sex-specific epidemiological pattern, with a smaller gap between incidence and mortality compared to most European countries.

title: Isolation, Purification, and Comprehensive Flow Cytometry Assessment of Lung Stromal Cells
creator: Sophia Rottmann, Veronika Lukacs‐Kornek
description: Stromal cells are non‐hematopoietic cells that consist of endothelial cells and various mesenchymal cell populations. The composition of the stromal cell compartment is diverse in different organs. Numerous recent studies demonstrated that the lung environment contains heterogeneous mesenchymal stromal cell populations with distinctive genomic signatures and location preferences.

title: Evolution of alpha-Gal synthesis - a growing risk for alpha Gal syndrome
creator: Rita Vaz-Rodrigues, José de la Fuente
description: BackgroundAlpha-Gal syndrome (AGS) is a growing burden worldwide associated with arthropods and allergies with pathologies such as urticaria, digestive and anaphylactic reactions. These reactions commonly appear 2–6 h after consumption of mammalian meat and derived pharmaceuticals mediated by immunoglobulin E against the oligosaccharide alpha-Gal epitope.

title: CARF regulates the alternative splicing and piwi/piRNA complexes during mouse spermatogenesis through PABPC1
creator: Yuming Cao, Shengnan Wang, Jie Liu, Jinfeng Xu, Yan Liang, Fei Ao, Zexiao Wei, Li Wang
description: ADP-ribosylation factor collaborator (CARF), which is also known as CDKN2AIP, was first recognized as an ADP-ribosylation factor-interacting protein that participates in the activation of the ARF-p53-p21 (WAF1) signaling pathway under different conditions, such as oxidative and oncogenic stresses. The activation of this pathway often leads to cell growth arrest and apoptosis as well as senescence.

title: Preoperative HALP index as a predictor of in-hospital mortality after type A aortic dissection surgery: a retrospective cohort study
creator: Zhen Chen, Zongxiang Lin, Qiuxia Liu, Pengfei Chen, Hao Chen
description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the predictive value of the preoperative haemoglobin–albumin–lymphocyte–platelet (HALP) index for in-hospital mortality in patients undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB)-assisted type A aortic dissection surgery.MethodsThis single-centre retrospective cohort study enrolled 750 adult patients who underwent type A aortic dissection surgery with CPB at a tertiary hospital from January 2021 to December 2025.

title: Involving People With Lived Experience in Electronic Health Record Database Studies Reflections and Learning From the CHOOSE Study
creator: Emma Cockcroft, Vidhi Bassi, Pearl L. H. Mok, Alex Adams, Anabel A. Claro, Alex M. Trafford, Matthew J. Carr, Darren M. Ashcroft, Emma Garavini, Rachel Temple, Roger T. Webb, Shruti Garg, Carolyn A. Chew‐Graham
description: BackgroundPatient and public involvement and engagement (PPIE) is integral to health research. Reporting of PPIE methods and impact is becoming increasingly common in health research. However, reporting on PPIE in studies using large, routinely collected electronic health record data sets is less common.

title: Microglial Expression of Serotonin Receptors Reveals Parallel Regulation of 5-HT2b and BDNF in the Rat Hippocampus
creator: Andrei Turkin, Maria Sidorova, Ekaterina Kurilova, Natalia Alenina, Oksana Tuchina, Friederike Klempin
description: Highlights What are the main findings? Transient, region-specific microglial 5-HTR expression;Upregulated microglial 5-HT2b in Tph2−/− rats parallels BDNF levels. What are the implications of the main findings? Temporal differences in 5-HTR signaling may drive adaptive responses to serotonin deficiency, with BDNF compensating at the later stage;Interplay between microglial serotonin and BDNF highlights potential targets for interventions in neuroinflammation.

title: Antibiotic pretreatment with ampicillin or streptomycin differentially shapes Salmonella infection kinetics and associated intestinal inflammation in mice
creator: Luca Maurer, Ursina Enz, Ersin Gül, Patrick Kiefer, Philipp Christen, Lea Fuchs, Wolf-Dietrich Hardt
description: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium (S. Tm) mouse infection models commonly rely on antibiotic pretreatment to disrupt microbiota-mediated colonization resistance and enable reproducible infection. Streptomycin is the primary antibiotic used, but alternative pretreatment regimens like ampicillin are increasingly employed, particularly for infections with attenuated S. Tm mutants.

title: Awareness level of cancer risk factors and warning signs among adults in Mansoura District, Egypt
creator: Ahmed M Eid, Abeer M Kamal, Asmaa Elsayed, Rahma M Almetwaly, Basma Kamel, Naira A Shoman, Aya M Abdelmohsin, Sara H Elhendawy, Yasmeen A State, C. A. collaboration team, Ahmed Mohamed Zayed, Abdel-Hady El-Gilany
description: BackgroundCancer remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with prevention and early detection dependent on the public awareness of its risk factors and warning signs. However, knowledge of cancer-related symptoms and modifiable risk factors remains limited in many populations, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Limited research exists examining general cancer awareness in Egypt's general population.

title: Clinical performance of a giomer-based pit and fissure sealant with and without air-abrasion pretreatment: a 12-month randomized clinical trial
creator: Yomna Sayed Khallaf, Olfat Elsayed Hassanein, Aya Mohamed Adly, Dina Kamal
description: BackgroundPit and fissure sealants are widely used for caries prevention; however, their long-term success depends largely on retention. Giomer-based sealants containing surface pre-reacted glass ionomer fillers offer bioactive properties, yet concerns remain regarding their bonding durability when applied with mild self-etch primers.

title: Exploration of In Situ Extraction for Enhanced Triterpenoid Production by Saccharomyces cerevisiae
creator: Mariam Dianat, Sarah Straaten, Aldo Maritato, Daniel Wibberg, Tobias Busche, Lars M. Blank, Birgitta E. Ebert
description: Plant‐derived triterpenoids are in high demand due to their valuable applications in cosmetic, nutraceutical, and pharmaceutical industries. To meet this demand, microbial production of triterpenoids is being developed for large‐scale production. However, a prominent limitation of microbial synthesis is the intracellular accumulation, requiring cell disruption during downstream processing.

title: Physiotherapists' Experiences and Perceived Acceptability of Delivering a Knee Bracing Intervention for People With Symptomatic Knee Osteoarthritis in a Randomised Trial (PROP OA): A Qualitative Study
creator: Laurna Bullock, Melanie A Holden, Clare Jinks, Evans Atiah Asamane, Dan Herron, Belinda Borrelli, Michael J Callaghan, Fraser Birrell, Nicola Halliday, Michelle Marshall, Gail Sowden, Carol Ingram, John McBeth, Krysia Dziedzic, Nadine E Foster, Sue Jowett, Sarah Lawton, Christian D Mallen, George Pe
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectivesTo explore physiotherapists' experiences and perceived acceptability of delivering a bracing intervention for knee osteoarthritis (OA) in the ‘PROvision of braces for Patients with knee OA’ (PROP OA) randomised controlled trial.MethodSemi‐structured telephone interviews with consenting physiotherapists who received the PROP OA training programme and delivered the knee bracing intervention (advice, information and exercise instruction plus knee brace matched to patients' clinical and radiographic presentation and with adherence support). Interviews were recorded and transcribed verbatim.

title: A dimeric mRNA vaccine based on key-mutant and KP.3 RBDs induces broad-spectrum immunity and protects mice against JN.1 and XDV challenges
creator: Jiali Xu, Rui Peng, Longhai Yuan, Huan Zhang, Cong Tang, Yanan Zhou, Hao Yang, Yun Yang, Qing Huang, Junbin Wang, Hongyu Chen, Wenqi Quan, Baisheng Li, Qiangming Sun, Shuaiyao Lu
description: The continued antigenic evolution of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron subvariants has progressively eroded vaccine-elicited protective immunity, driving demand for next-generation candidates that confer broad-spectrum protection against phylogenetically divergent strains. Here we report the design and preclinical evaluation of SV, an mRNA vaccine encoding a heterodimeric receptor-binding domain (RBD) antigen.

title: Comparative analysis on rhizosphere microorganisms of Cynodon dactylon (Poaceae) from the natural restoration area and eco-restoration engineering area in water-level-fluctuation zone of Jinsha River-type reservoirs, China
creator: Lanfang Zhou, Shengjun Wu, Maohua Ma
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Rhizosphere microorganisms may play an important role in plant growth and environmental adaptation during eco-restoration engineering in the water-level-fluctuation zone (WLFZ) of large river-type reservoirs. The purpose of this study is to compare the rhizosphere microbial community features of Cynodon dactylon derived from the natural restoration area (NEE) and eco-restoration engineering area (YEE) in the WLFZ of Jinsha River-type reservoirs using high-throughput sequencing and bioinformatic analyses. The dominant taxa were Proteobacteria and Ascomycota in C. dactylon rhizosphere from both NEE and YEE.

title: Laser scanning registration for knee arthroplasty
creator: Thomas Warren, Ulani Hayter Otaola, Brett Robertson, Riaz Khan, Sam Withers, Hari Goonatillake, Benjamin Hewitt, Tomasz Kozak, Sajan Kuriakose, Tareq Batanony, Jon Greenwald, Morteza Meftah
description: AimsAccurate registration of anatomy is fundamental to robotic and computer-assisted surgery; however, conventional methods rely on manual data acquisition performed by the surgeon using a tracked probe that is slow and affected by operator variability. Limitations of manual methods have hindered wider adoption of surgical navigation despite its benefits for alignment accuracy, particularly in orthopaedic applications.

title: 铁死亡在主动脉夹层中的作用研究进展
creator: Xiang HONG, Yuchong ZHANG, Weiguo FU, Lixin WANG, 敏 沈, 丽娜 刘
description: 近年来研究发现，由氧化应激等刺激因素导致的铁代谢紊乱与脂质过氧化诱导的铁死亡在主动脉夹层的发生和发展中发挥重要作用。其中，铁代谢紊乱主要体现为铁含量与血红素代谢异常导致的羟基自由基过量生成，而脂质过氧化则与Xc－系统异常及磷脂氢过氧化物过量积累相关。这些因素协同导致主动脉稳态被破坏，驱动主动脉夹层中内皮细胞和血管平滑肌细胞等管壁组成细胞铁死亡。主动脉夹层中存在多个铁死亡相关基因紊乱，且吸烟等流行病学因素、蛋白质甲基化等表观遗传修饰及T淋巴细胞等免疫细胞功能异常亦与主动脉夹层铁死亡密切相关。此外，一些小分子药物和纳米材料显示出一定的抑制主动脉夹层铁死亡效果。本文通过探讨主动脉夹层铁死亡的潜在机制，旨在为主动脉夹层精准防治提供策略。Keywords: 主动脉夹层, 铁死亡, 发病机制, 综述 主动脉夹层是一种严重威胁生命的心血管疾病，在我国的年发病率约为3/10万［1］。血管平滑肌细胞、血管内皮细胞和包括巨噬细胞在内的免疫细胞等主动脉管壁主要组成细胞的功能改变、损伤乃至死亡会直接导致管壁结构薄弱和微环境稳态失衡，是主动脉夹层发病和持续进展的重要原因［2-4］。调节性细胞死亡是一类在调控机制上完全不同的细胞死亡形式，其共同特征是受分子和信号机制的严格调控。其中，铁死亡作为一种以铁代谢紊乱和脂质过氧化为主要特征的铁依赖性调节性细胞死亡形式，在促进包括主动脉夹层、腹主动脉瘤和动脉粥样硬化等血管疾病中发挥关键作用，并且可作为潜在的干预靶点［5-6］。主动脉夹层中主动脉管壁组成细胞如血管平滑肌细胞、血管内皮细胞等管壁细胞的丢失是铁死亡、凋亡、坏死和自噬等多种复杂因素共同作用的结果［7］。有学者通过对高通量基因表达（Gene Expression Omnibus）数据库中的人体Stanford A型主动脉夹层资料分析发现，主动脉夹层组织中铁死亡富集评分显著高于正常主动脉组织，且铁死亡富集评分高于铜死亡、细胞焦亡、免疫原性细胞死亡、坏死性凋亡和自噬的富集评分［8］，提示铁死亡相关基因的表达倍数变化可能是人体主动脉夹层组织中导致细胞死亡的核心原因之一。本文重点概述了铁死亡促进主动脉夹层发生和进展的潜在机制，并对存在的问题和发展方向进行展望，以促进主动脉夹层中铁死亡研究的临床转化。 铁死亡参与主动脉夹层的病理过程 有研究发现，主动脉夹层患者组织中存在显著的铁超载和脂质过氧化现象，同时伴多个氧化还原调节枢纽基因表达的严重紊乱，其典型表现为铁蛋白和脂质过氧化终产物4-羟基壬烯醛等在主动脉中层区域显著上调［9-10］。另外，Tao等［11］发现主动脉夹层患者的主动脉尤其内皮细胞中铁死亡驱动基因PTGS2的蛋白质表达量显著增加，而铁死亡抑制基因GPX4的蛋白质表达量显著减少。进一步提示铁死亡与主动脉夹层密切相关，且影响了位于主动脉内层和中层的内皮细胞以及血管平滑肌细胞等多种细胞类型，直接参与了主动脉夹层发生发展的病理过程。 β-氨基丙腈是一种赖氨酰氧化酶的强效抑制剂。β-氨基丙腈诱导的小鼠主动脉夹层模型是夹层发病机制研究的经典模型。β-氨基丙腈可诱导小鼠主动脉出现明显的中层变性、血管平滑肌细胞丢失和弹性纤维断裂［12］。研究发现，小鼠经β-氨基丙腈处理后主动脉中铁死亡驱动基因表达会随着主动脉的退变而显著上调，同时脂质过氧化产物含量也会显著增加，而这种负面效应可以被铁死亡特异性抑制剂消除［9-10］。上述研究共同提示，铁死亡是主动脉夹层中导致主动脉内层和中层退变并使疾病持续进展的重要原因，是导致主动脉管壁血管平滑肌细胞和内皮细胞死亡的重要调节性细胞死亡形式。 主动脉夹层铁死亡的驱动因素 铁代谢紊乱导致主动脉夹层铁死亡 细胞铁稳态受铁的摄取、利用、储存和排泄这几个环节共同调节维持。食物摄入以及血红素的降解是机体中铁的两大主要来源。血液中铁离子可与转铁蛋白结合形成复合物，而转铁蛋白可被转铁蛋白受体识别，铁离子通过转铁蛋白受体介导的内吞作用以转铁蛋白-铁离子的形式被转运到细胞内部，而细胞内过量铁则以铁离子的形式储存在铁蛋白中，或经细胞膜铁转运蛋白从细胞中转运至细胞外而被清除，若亚铁离子不能被及时转运清除出细胞，而是在细胞内过度积累，则会触发芬顿反应，将过氧化氢转化为氧化性极强的羟基自由基，最终导致细胞发生脂质过氧化和铁死亡［13-14］。 铁含量异常与主动脉夹层铁死亡关系 主动脉夹层患者的血清或组织中铁含量较正常人群均呈上升趋势，其中主动脉夹层组织铁含量几乎是正常人群主动脉组织的两倍［15］。与正常组织比较，主动脉夹层组织中转铁蛋白受体的mRNA和蛋白质水平均上调，铁蛋白含量增加，同时主动脉中总铁含量和亚铁离子含量均增加［9-10］。有研究对主动脉夹层患者的外周血和组织中的铁代谢相关生物标志物分析发现，Stanford A型和Stanford B型主动脉夹层的发生风险与血液中铁离子浓度均呈负相关，且患者血清中转铁蛋白、总铁结合力和转铁蛋白饱和度的水平均低于正常人群，同时主动脉组织中的转铁蛋白水平也较正常人群更低［16-17］。上述研究提示，铁大量摄入或体内亚铁离子过量积聚可能会诱发主动脉夹层铁死亡，同时导致疾病持续进展。 然而，与单纯使用AngⅡ刺激比较，缺铁饮食联合AngⅡ刺激诱导的小鼠主动脉损伤模型的主动脉中层退变进一步加剧，其原因为缺铁可通过破坏血管平滑肌细胞骨架从而引发血管平滑肌细胞表型转换和诱导线粒体过度分裂，促进主动脉夹层的发生和发展［16-17］。Shi等［18］发现类似结果：患者主动脉夹层组织中转铁蛋白水平降低、转铁蛋白受体和铁转运蛋白水平升高；在缺铁饮食喂养联合AngⅡ刺激的主动脉损伤模型小鼠中主动脉组织铁离子水平显著降低，且缺铁程度与内质网应激、线粒体氧化应激和主动脉中膜细胞凋亡水平呈正相关。 目前，铁过量或铁缺乏与主动脉夹层之间的因果关系尚未明确，甚至在不同研究中出现完全相反的结论［8，16］。如转铁蛋白受体在功能上作为铁进入细胞的关键门户，其在主动脉夹层组织中的水平上升可能是介导铁死亡发生的关键因素之一。然而，有研究发现在小鼠中进行转铁蛋白受体基因敲除会导致其胚胎纯合致死伴主动脉结构异常，而杂合子并不受影响［16］。这些现象共同提示铁代谢与主动脉夹层铁死亡的关系本质上是一个铁稳态的调节过程，无论铁过量或是铁缺乏均会导致主动脉夹层发生风险增加，诱发主动脉结构的严重退变。 基于铁元素及其代谢在维持主动脉稳态中的关键作用，已尝试血清铁、转铁蛋白等在内的外周血生物标志物作为鉴别诊断主动脉夹层与冠心病的重要指标（FLUTHE模型），其诊断敏感度为0.954、特异度达0.905，提示铁代谢紊乱和铁死亡在主动脉夹层发病机制中发挥重要作用［19］。 血红素代谢异常与主动脉夹层铁死亡关系 HO-1是体内降解血红素的关键酶。细胞处于缺氧、氧化应激或其他微环境变化时会强烈诱导HO-1产生［20］。HIF-1是一种响应缺氧调节氧稳态的重要转录因子，其活性亚基为HIF-1α［21］。HO-1和HIF-1α在人体主动脉夹层标本中的表达均显著上调，且氧化应激可通过HIF-1α/HO-1轴诱导血管平滑肌细胞发生铁死亡［8］。具体来说，HIF-1α可驱动靶基因HO-1在血管平滑肌细胞中过量表达，使主动脉夹层部位大量血红素降解产生游离铁，游离铁又可进一步通过芬顿反应产生大量羟基自由基，介导铁超载、铁死亡和氧化应激的恶性循环［22］。由于主动脉夹层发生后大量血液冲击进入管壁形成血栓，其中大量血红素被HO-1分解，故HO-1在主动脉夹层中具有重要效应。Shi等［23］的研究发现，由胱氨酸剥夺或IKE诱导铁死亡的HASMC中内源性组蛋白乙酰转移酶P300蛋白水平均显著降低，P300缺乏又可激活HIF-1α/HO-1通路，是HASMC最终发生铁死亡的重要原因之一。该研究再次证实HIF-1α/HO-1轴是主动脉夹层铁死亡的关键驱动因素。 尽管HO-1具备通过增强铁释放而促铁死亡的能力，但有研究认为血红素是一种强促氧化剂，可加剧炎症反应并促进细胞死亡，而HO-1可通过分解血红素起到细胞保护作用［24］。Liao等［25］将HO-1蛋白表达水平的下调作为主动脉夹层铁死亡发生的标志之一。这与Song等［8］和Shi等［23］认为HO-1上调可在主动脉夹层中导致铁死亡发生的研究结论不一致。其主要原因可能是所选择的血管平滑肌细胞铁死亡诱导剂不同，且HO-1可能存在代偿与失代偿的平衡紊乱。由此可见，尽管包括过氧化氢、胱氨酸剥夺、IKE和AngⅡ等在内的多种刺激因素均可引起血管平滑肌细胞铁死亡，但其潜在分子机制并不完全一致。提示在细胞层面进行铁死亡相关研究时，必须谨慎考虑不同外源性刺激因素的差异对结果造成的潜在影响，且无论在细胞水平施加哪一种外源性刺激因素，可能均无法准确还原患者来源主动脉夹层的体内病理学特征。 脂质过氧化导致主动脉夹层铁死亡 除铁代谢紊乱外，主动脉夹层铁死亡的另一个基本要素是脂质过氧化。多不饱和脂肪酸和磷脂酰乙醇胺是脂质过氧化的两个主要底物，其中磷脂酰乙醇胺含有花生四烯酸或其衍生物肾上腺素。研究发现多不饱和脂肪酸和磷脂酰乙醇胺的氧化共同传递了铁死亡信号。花生四烯酸可先通过ACSL4转化为花生四烯酸-辅酶A，并进一步转化为磷脂酰乙醇胺-花生四烯酸，最终被氧化为脂质过氧化底物［26-27］。高静水压或AngⅡ刺激下血管平滑肌细胞中ACSL4表达均显著上调，这是导致血管平滑肌细胞铁死亡的重要原因；而抑制ACSL4可减少细胞内脂质过氧化物底物的积累，从而抑制铁死亡［28-29］。 Xc－系统和GPX4是主动脉夹层铁死亡中脂质过氧化的核心抑制因素。Xc－系统是谷氨酸/胱氨酸逆向转运蛋白，为轻链亚基SLC7A11和重链亚基SLC3A2组成的异二聚体。其中SLC7A11介导Xc－系统的蛋白转运活性，而SLC3A2的主要功能是保持SLC7A11蛋白稳定性［30］。Xc－系统可将细胞外胱氨酸转运到细胞质中，用于合成谷胱甘肽，后者是保护细胞免受氧化应激损伤的重要还原剂。在铁死亡诱导剂胱氨酸剥夺、IKE和GPX4抑制剂RSL3刺激的HASMC中，SLC7A11和SLC3A2蛋白水平均显著下调，Xc－系统被抑制并阻碍谷胱甘肽合成，谷胱甘肽缺乏会直接抑制GPX4活性并导致磷脂氢过氧化物过量积累，最终铁死亡和主动脉稳态破坏［9-10］。除Xc－系统和GPX4外，FSP1、GTP环化水解酶1和二氢乳清酸脱氢酶等也是在主动脉夹层中介导磷脂氢过氧化物清除、抑制脂质过氧化的重要效应分子［23，31］。 其他导致主动脉夹层铁死亡的因素 主动脉夹层铁死亡相关基因 Pan等［32］基于主动脉夹层患者的高通量测序数据鉴定出Stanford A型主动脉夹层中的核心铁死亡相关基因为DAZAP1和GABARAPL2，其中DAZAP1是一种广泛表达的RNA结合蛋白，在蛋白质转录后修饰中发挥重要作用；GABARAPL2因参与蛋白质转运和膜融合等而被发现；进一步免疫浸润分析提示，DAZAP1表达水平与单核细胞丰度呈正相关，而GABARAPL2表达则与单核细胞丰度呈负相关，两者均可作为Stanford A型主动脉夹层的潜在诊断生物标志物。Zou等［33］通过构建蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络，从Stanford A型主动脉夹层与正常主动脉组织之间差异表达的铁死亡相关基因中鉴定出CA9、HMOX1、IL-6、CDKN1A、HIF1A、MYC这六个关键基因，且上述基因在Stanford A型主动脉夹层中表达均上调。 吸烟导致主动脉夹层铁死亡 吸烟是主动脉夹层公认的危险因素之一［34］。研究发现，CSE刺激可使大鼠血管平滑肌细胞出现活性降低及死亡，而这种效应可被特异性铁死亡抑制剂或铁螯合剂完全抑制；CSE还可诱导脂质过氧化水平上调，并激活炎症和细胞内抗氧化物质谷胱甘肽的耗竭等铁死亡的关键特征［35］。Zou等［33］通过生物信息学方法筛选出CA9、IL-6、CDKN1A、HIF1A这四个主动脉夹层中的铁死亡相关基因，并在细胞水平验证这四个基因与CSE诱导的HASMC铁死亡密切相关。线粒体是细胞生物氧化的主要场所之一，线粒体在铁死亡时的典型形态学改变表现为膜密度增加，体积减小并伴有线粒体嵴的断裂和缺失［36］。通过透射电子显微镜可以观察到CSE处理的血管平滑肌细胞中线粒体大量丢失，仅剩少量残存的线粒体碎片，而经铁死亡抑制剂预处理的血管平滑肌细胞则表现出对CSE刺激的抗性，其线粒体结构也得到较完整的保留［35］。作为CSE中的核心成分，尼古丁被发现可以剂量依赖方式使人脐静脉内皮细胞发生铁死亡，同时可抑制GPX4表达，而铁死亡抑制剂Ferrostatin-1可抑制其促人脐静脉内皮细胞铁死亡的作用［11］。 表观遗传异常导致主动脉夹层铁死亡 非编码RNA、RNA甲基化、蛋白质甲基化等表观遗传学机制在主动脉夹层铁死亡中的作用越来越受到学界的关注［37］。miRNA是一种内源性非编码单链小RNA分子，miRNA可导致靶基因mRNA被切割或抑制该基因翻译，在包括主动脉夹层等心血管疾病的铁死亡中发挥重要的调控作用［38-39］。基于高通量筛选发现，miR-1909-5p能与抗铁死亡核心基因GPX4直接结合，从而分别在转录和蛋白水平负调控GPX4表达；过表达miR-1909-5p可加重尼古丁诱导的人脐静脉内皮细胞铁死亡，敲低miR-1909-5p或补充外源性的GPX4重组蛋白则可以一定程度上消除尼古丁的促铁死亡作用，提示miR-1909-5p对部分吸烟的主动脉夹层患者中内皮细胞的铁死亡具有重要意义［11］。lncRNA不编码蛋白质，是调节转录、翻译、修饰、RNA和蛋白质稳定性等关键生理病理过程的重要分子，在调控铁死亡和主动脉夹层等心血管疾病中具有重要作用［39-40］。其中，NORAD是一种高度保守的lncRNA，可通过调节GPX4抑制铁死亡，发挥主动脉夹层抑制作用［25］。RNA甲基转移酶METTL3又能够通过m6A修饰阅读蛋白YTHDF2依赖的方式来介导NORAD的m6A甲基化修饰，提示NORAD可以作为主动脉夹层的潜在治疗靶点。 此外，研究发现METTL3本身在主动脉夹层患者主动脉中的表达水平也显著上调，其蛋白质水平与人主动脉中的铁死亡抑制蛋白SLC7A11及FSP1的水平呈负相关。在HASMC中过表达METTL3会抑制SLC7A11和FSP1的表达，促进HASMC对铁死亡的敏感性；而敲低METTL3则可促进SLC7A11和FSP1的表达并增加HASMC对铁死亡的耐受能力［9］。 蛋白质甲基化同样是一种常见的蛋白质转录后修饰类型，其中组蛋白甲基化最为常见。有研究发现组蛋白甲基化参与调控了主动脉夹层铁死亡的病理过程［41］。胱氨酸剥夺、IKE或RSL3等铁死亡诱导剂处理的HASMC中组蛋白甲基化位点H3K9me1、H3K9me2和H3K9me3蛋白质水平均增加，表明H3K9甲基化是调控主动脉管壁铁死亡的关键表观遗传机制［10］。另外发现H3K4甲基化在主动脉夹层铁死亡中也发挥重要作用，组蛋白甲基化位点H3K4me1和H3K4me2蛋白质水平在β-氨基丙腈诱导的主动脉夹层小鼠中下降，并可进一步使细胞内亚铁离子大量沉积而引发剧烈的芬顿反应，最终导致铁死亡［31］。 免疫细胞功能异常导致主动脉夹层铁死亡 铁死亡与免疫系统功能异常存在密切关联［42］。T淋巴细胞是机体免疫应答系统的重要组成，幼稚T细胞在暴露于抗原后可分化为效应记忆T淋巴细胞，迁移并驻留至靶器官，这对于协调机体免疫反应至关重要［43］。Li等［44］研究了CD4+ T细胞在分化过程中的活化多样化对主动脉夹层铁死亡的作用和机制，发现主动脉夹层患者CD4+ T细胞中膜蛋白CD36表达比例显著上调，而CD36可通过摄取脂肪酸使CD4+ T细胞铁死亡增敏，导致CD4+ T细胞功能低下、线粒体丢失和分化功能受损，并与主动脉夹层患者术后不良预后相关。除T淋巴细胞外，巨噬细胞等其他类型的免疫细胞也与铁死亡进程密切相关［45］。巨噬细胞铁死亡研究在动脉粥样硬化和动脉瘤中已有相关报道［46-47］，与主动脉夹层潜在关联仍待阐明。 针对主动脉夹层铁死亡的干预策略 Ferrostatin-1是第一代铁死亡抑制剂。Dixon等［5］对可溶性化合物的小分子库进行高通量筛选，于2012年首次报道了Ferrostatin-1具有抗铁死亡的效果。在此基础上，Zilka等［48］通过化合物构效关系研究进一步阐明了Ferrostatin-1的抗氧化机制，发现其结构中的N-环己基可作为生物膜中的亲脂性锚，是Ferrostatin-1能够作为还原剂和抗氧化剂的重要结构基础，其对铁死亡的抑制能力至关重要。相关研究显示，Ferrostatin-1能维持胱氨酸剥夺、IKE和RSL3诱导HASMC的细胞活性，同时可以下调HO-1水平、抑制脂质过氧化并防止铁死亡［10］。Ferrostatin-1也可以在CSE诱导的大鼠胸大动脉平滑肌细胞A7r5和血管平滑肌细胞中显著抑制铁死亡，防止CSE刺激下小鼠主动脉血管平滑肌细胞的大量丢失［35］。然而，由于Ferrostatin-1在血浆和代谢过程中的不稳定性，其在体内的实际疗效可能弱于在体外实验中展现的水平［49］。Liproxstatin-1也是一种铁死亡的特异性抑制剂，最早是从他莫昔芬诱导的Gpx4－/－ 小鼠胚胎成纤维细胞中筛选获得［50］。Zilka等［51］证实Liproxstatin-1与Ferrostatin-1类似，具有较强的自由基捕获抗氧化活性，而喹喔啉环是其清除过氧自由基的关键基团。Liproxstatin-1可以抑制β-氨基丙腈诱导的小鼠主动脉夹层的发展和破裂，同时下调转铁蛋白受体、HO-1等铁死亡标志物，证明Liproxstatin-1具有良好的体内抑制主动脉夹层铁死亡能力［9］。 另外，HIF-1α在主动脉夹层铁死亡发挥重要驱动因素，其高表达与主动脉夹层微环境中的氧化应激压力存在密切关联［8］。Shi等［23］发现HIF-1α抑制剂BAY87-2243可显著下调HIF-1α水平，抑制胱氨酸剥夺和IKE所引发HASMC铁死亡，提高细胞活性并减少脂质过氧化，还需要在体内试验进行验证。 鉴于组蛋白甲基化在主动脉夹层中的潜在作用，国内学者发现组蛋白甲基化位点H3K9me1/2/3的抑制剂BRD4770可显著抑制HASMC铁死亡，且其疗效与Ferrostatin-1相当。BRD4770还可通过抑制铁死亡、脂质过氧化和炎症共同延缓β-氨基丙腈诱导小鼠主动脉夹层的发生和发展［10］。由于组蛋白甲基化位点H3K4me1和H3K4me2的蛋白质水平在小鼠主动脉夹层中降低，有学者筛选出特异性药物SP2509，能靶向作用于H3K4me1和H3K4me2，以黄素腺嘌呤二核苷酸依赖的方式使H3K4去甲基化［52］。SP2509可上调主动脉夹层中组蛋白甲基化位点H3K4me1和H3K4me2的蛋白质水平，通过调节铁转运降低细胞内亚铁离子水平，从而阻止HASMC发生铁死亡［31］。 值得注意的是，尽管许多小分子化合物呈现出较好的体外抑制铁死亡效果，但其在体内降解速度快、治疗效率低等缺陷可能限制了转化应用。有学者提出了一种可以持续缓释间充质干细胞来源外泌体的三维打印水凝胶体系，通过预防主动脉结构变性和铁死亡实现主动脉夹层的药物治疗［53］。这类基于特定纳米材料的交叉研究提供了针对性干预主动脉夹层铁死亡的全新视角。 结语 综上所述，现有研究已证明铁死亡在主动脉夹层中具有重要作用（图1），相关分子机制的阐明可能为主动脉夹层提供新的精准干预靶点。未来可从以下几点开展进一步研究：①当前主动脉夹层铁死亡中的靶点多数已在其他心血管疾病或肿瘤中报道，今后应运用多组学手段和高通量筛选技术对主动脉夹层铁死亡新的生物标志物进行识别和验证，鉴定出主动脉夹层铁死亡特异性靶点。②主动脉夹层的发生是一个主动脉退变逐渐累积产生的结果，只有证明在主动脉夹层发生前存在铁超载和脂质过氧化等特征，铁死亡才能被证实是主动脉夹层发生和进展的驱动因素。由于当前动物模型和临床标本的限制，目前研究中采用铁死亡抑制药物与造模药物同时干预，故铁死亡与主动脉夹层的因果关系尚不明确。因此，有必要进一步探究如主动脉夹层造模不同阶段，β-氨基丙腈和AngⅡ等不同主动脉夹层造模方式以及小鼠不同种属、年龄和性别等变量对主动脉夹层铁死亡的影响。随着全基因组关联研究在全球的开展，如孟德尔随机化等方法同样可能有助于验证铁死亡与主动脉夹层之间的联系。③Ferrostatin-1等药物存在体内代谢不稳定等不足，miRNA和lncRNA等核酸类物质作为药物也存在递送效率低、稳定性差易被核酸酶降解等诸多不足［54］。纳米医学在主动脉夹层等主动脉疾病的抗氧化应激和精准递送小分子化合物或核酸类物质等方面已展现出相当的潜力［53，55-56］。故通过结合相关技术或可促进主动脉夹层铁死亡相关的机制研究和治疗靶点的转化。④针对主动脉夹层铁死亡过程中的关键微环境组分如铁离子等开发特异性诊断工具、研制基于铁死亡的主动脉夹层快速诊断试剂盒也是一个极具前景的研究方向［57］。 铁死亡在主动脉夹层中的核心调控机制（采用Figdraw绘制） 主动脉夹层铁死亡的过程与铁代谢、脂质代谢和氨基酸代谢三种重要代谢过程有关. 转铁蛋白通过细胞膜上的转铁蛋白受体与细胞结合，以铁离子的形式摄取，铁离子被还原为亚铁离子，再被转运到细胞质中的不稳定铁池. 大部分亚铁离子可由铁调素受体蛋白释放出细胞，或储存在FTH和FTL中；剩余亚铁离子可能通过芬顿反应转化生成活性氧. ACSL4催化PUFA转化为PL-PUFA，活性氧积累会使PL-PUFA过氧化，引起铁死亡.

title: Effects of a 12-week combined exercise-nutrition intervention on body composition, physical fitness, and lifestyle disease indicators in women with normal weight obesity
creator: Dasom Heo, Man-Gyoon Lee, Won-Sang Jung
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). [Purpose]This study investigated the effects of 12 weeks of nutrition education and combined exercise training on body composition, physical fitness, and lifestyle disease indicators in women with normal weight obesity (NWO).[Methods]Twenty-six women with NWO in their 30s (BMI 18.5-22.9 kg/m2, body fat ≥ 30%) were randomly assigned to either a diet education and exercise training group (DE+TR; n = 13) or a diet education only group (DE; n = 13).

title: Analgesic mechanism of Panaphix in spinal nerve-ligated rats: involvement of microglial inflammatory cytokines
creator: Myong-Hwan Karm, Hyun-Jung Kwon, Doo-Hwan Kim, Jun-Seok Lee, Minsu Han, Eun Ha Kim, Chan-Sik Kim, Jin-Woo Shin, Seong-Soo Choi
description: BackgroundNeuropathic pain, a chronic and debilitating condition caused by damage to the nervous system, remains challenging to treat due to its complex pathophysiology and resistance to analgesics. This study investigated the analgesic effects of Panaphix (PAX-1), a novel pharmacological agent, in a rat model of neuropathic pain induced by spinal nerve ligation (SNL).

title: Validation of the arabic multidimensional facebook intensity scale and its relationships with life satisfaction, happiness, and physical activity
creator: Hilmi Jelleli, Nashwan Nashwan, Omar Hindawi, Mohamed Ben Aissa, Mahmoud Rebhi, Wiem Melki, Mouna Saidane, Noomen Guelmami, Tore Bonsaksen
description: [Purpose]Despite Facebook’s widespread use in Arab countries, validated Arabic tools to assess the intensity of its use and related psychological and behavioral outcomes are lacking. This study aims to validate the Arabic version of the Multidimensional Facebook Intensity Scale (A-MFIS) and examine its associations with life satisfaction, happiness, and physical activity in a large Tunisian adult sample.

title: Utilization of EGFR, ALK, and BRAF Inhibitors in the Treatment of Lung Cancer in Germany
creator: Nikolaj Rischke, Josephine Kanbach, Ulrike Haug
description: BackgroundThere is a lack of real‐world data on the use of targeted cancer drugs requiring molecular tumor diagnostics in the treatment of lung cancer in Germany.AimsWe aimed to characterize the use of such drugs in lung cancer patients based on longitudinal analyses.

title: Multiscale spatial analysis implicates chromosomal metaloops in gene patterning across the Drosophila brain
creator: Aleena L. Patel, Achuthan Raja Venkatesh, Tohn Borjigin, Xiao Li, Michael S. Levine, Alistair N. Boettiger
description: Scores of chromosome-scale loops, or metaloops, arise in the Drosophila brain, but their spatial organization and relationship to neural gene expression patterns remain unclear. Here, we used multiplexed Optical Reconstruction of Chromatin Architecture (ORCA) to examine the multiscale spatial organization of metaloops in cross-sections of 100s of larval and adult Drosophila brains.

title: A Deep Learning Network for Accurate Retinal Multidisease Diagnosis Using Multiview Fusion of En Face and B-Scan Images: A Multicenter Study
creator: Chubin Ou, Xifei Wei, Lin An, Jia Qin, Min Zhu, Mei Jin, Xiangbin Kong
description: PurposeAccurate diagnosis of retinal disease based on optical coherence tomography (OCT) requires scrutiny of both B-scan and en face images. The aim of this study was to investigate the effectiveness of fusing en face and B-scan images for better diagnostic performance of deep learning models.

title: CryptoBench: cryptic protein–ligand binding sites dataset and benchmark
creator: Vít Škrhák, Marian Novotný, Christos P Feidakis, Radoslav Krivák, David Hoksza
description: MotivationStructure-based methods for detecting protein–ligand binding sites play a crucial role in various domains, from fundamental research to biomedical applications. However, current prediction methodologies often rely on holo (ligand-bound) protein conformations for training and evaluation, overlooking the significance of the apo (ligand-free) states.

title: Sex-Specific Dominance of Gene Expression in Seed Beetles
creator: Philipp Kaufmann, Johanna Liljestrand Rönn, Elina Immonen, Göran Arnqvist
description: When different alleles are favored in different environments, dominance reversal where alternate alleles are dominant in the environment in which they are favored can generate net balancing selection. The sexes represent two distinct genetic environments and sexually antagonistic (SA) selection can maintain genetic variation, especially when the alleles involved show sex-specific dominance.

title: Histone H3K9 methylation and Heterochromatin Protein 1 do not limit DNA accessibility in living S. pombe cells
creator: Lalita Panigrahi, Zhuwei Xu, David J Clark
description: Chromatin is intrinsically repressive, limiting access to DNA, implying a major regulatory role. Studies with nuclei support this model. title: Biological Features of KLC2 Mutations in Chronic Myeloid Leukemia and Their Contribution to Inducing Drug Resistance
creator: Rabindranath Bera, Yotaro Ochi, Ying-Jung Huang, Ming-Chung Kuo, Kenichi Yoshida, Seishi Ogawa, Lee-Yung Shih
description: BackgroundBreakpoint Cluster Region-Abelson (BCR::ABL1) fusion protein is essential in the pathogenesis of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML); however, the chronic-to-blast phase transformation remains elusive. We identified novel kinesin light chain 2 (KLC2) mutations in CML-myeloid blast phase patients. We aimed to examine the functional role of KLC2 mutations in leukemogenesis.

title: Monitoring Over Time of Pathological Complete Response to Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Breast Cancer Patients Through an Ensemble Vision Transformers‐Based Model
creator: Maria Colomba Comes, Annarita Fanizzi, Samantha Bove, Luca Boldrini, Agnese Latorre, Deniz Can Guven, Serena Iacovelli, Tiziana Talienti, Alessandro Rizzo, Francesco Alfredo Zito, Raffaella Massafra
description: BackgroundMorphological and vascular characteristics of breast cancer can change during neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC). Dynamic contrast‐enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE‐MRI)‐acquired pre‐ and mid‐treatment quantitatively capture information about tumor heterogeneity as potential earlier indicators of pathological complete response (pCR) to NAC in breast cancer.

title: Impact of Clinical Characteristics and Treatment on Cholangiocarcinoma Prognosis in Southern Thailand
creator: Chirawadee Sathitruangsak, Tanawat Pattarapuntakul, Apichat Kaewdech, Tortrakoon Thongkan, Apinya Prisutkul, Phatcharaporn Thongwatchara, Hutcha Sriplung, Chanon Kongkamol, Kanyanatt Kanokwiroon, Sumalee Obchoei, Pimsiri Sripongpun
description: BackgroundCholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is most commonly seen in Northeastern Thailand and other parts of Asia where liver flukes are prevalent. However, it is unknown whether CCA patients in low and high liver fluke prevalence areas are similar. This study aimed to analyze the clinical characteristics and outcomes of CCA patients in Southern Thailand.

title: Structures of pUG-fold RNA bound to DNMT1 reveal a mechanism for RNA-mediated epigenetic regulation
creator: Jessica J. Song, Thomas R. Cech, Vignesh Kasinath
description: Many chromatin-associated proteins have been found to bind RNA as a means of epigenetic regulation. Specifically, DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1), which maintains cytosine methylation at CpG dinucleotides, is inhibited by RNA at transcribed DNA loci in cells. However, the mechanisms by which RNA binds DNMT1 and inhibits its activity remain unknown.

title: Development of Patient-Derived Conditionally Reprogrammed 3D Breast Cancer Culture Models for Drug Sensitivity Evaluation
creator: Jing Cai, Haoyun Zhu, Weiling Guo, Ting Huang, Pangzhou Chen, Wen Zhou, Ziyun Guan
description: BackgroundTherapeutic responses of breast cancer vary among patients and lead to drug resistance and recurrence due to the heterogeneity. Current preclinical models, however, are inadequate for predicting individual patient responses towards different drugs. This study aimed to investigate the patient-derived breast cancer culture models for drug sensitivity evaluations.MethodsTumor and adjacent tissues from female breast cancer patients were collected during surgery.

title: Epidemiology of asymptomatic peptic ulcer disease diagnosed during screening endoscopy in patients with cirrhosis
creator: Girma Deshimo Lema, Enguday Demeke Gebeyaw
description: ObjectiveAsymptomatic peptic ulcer disease (PUD) is frequently overlooked in patients with cirrhosis, who are at increased risk for gastrointestinal complications that can lead to increased morbidity and mortality. title: The Use of Baclofen to Control Vertical Nystagmus in a Patient with Advanced Glioma: A Case Report
creator: Luma Alfraihat, Sami Ayed Alshammary, Hassan Yousef Alghar
description: Nystagmus, characterized by involuntary eye movements, can arise from several causes, with benign paroxysmal positional vertigo being the most prevalent. Additionally, central lesions such as tumors may also induce nystagmus. This case report describes the amelioration of vertical nystagmus in a patient with advanced glioma after treatment with the GABAergic drug baclofen.

title: Integrated Pan-Cancer Profiling and Breast Cancer Validation Identify BEND3 as a Potential Prognostic and Immune Biomarker
creator: Yuting Gou, Yongxiang Li, Yiyang Wang, Haotian Ma, Haocong Li, Reyima Geni, Dilimulati Ismtula, Chenming Guo
description: PurposeBEND3 is implicated in various physiological processes, including chromatin regulation, cell cycle regulation, etc.; nonetheless, its function in cancer is not well comprehended.MethodsUsing public databases including UCSC Xena, TCGA, GTEx, and GEO, we conducted a comprehensive pan-cancer analysis to evaluate the clinical relevance of BEND3 across 33 cancer types.

title: Pressure Reactivity Index - Daily in Pediatric Traumatic Brain Injury
creator: Suresh Nathan, Farooqi Ahmed, Michael Wolf, Prout Andrew, Ajit Sarnaik
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Purpose Pressure Reactivity Index (PRx) is a measure of cerebral autoregulation that is associated with outcomes in pediatric traumatic brain injury. It is a resource-intensive tool that is not universally available. This study aims to assess the association of a novel low-resolution index derived from the same physiological inputs as the PRx, termed the Pressure Reactivity Index-Daily (PRx-D), with outcomes in children with traumatic brain injury (TBI).

title: Reorganization of Long-Term Care Insurance for End-of-Life Care
creator: Hyunjong Song
description: Korea introduced long-term care insurance on July 1, 2008, to alleviate the burden on families caring for older adults amidst rapid aging and societal changes. Since then, the system has expanded significantly. However, there remains a shortfall in services adequately addressing the nursing, care, health, and medical needs of older adults at the end of life.

The objective of this study is to elucidate the potential correlation between PM‐RGs and DN.MethodsDN‐related datasets and 59 PM‐RGs were obtained from the public database.

title: From the archives: Roles of microtubule-associated proteins in organelle movement, tip growth, and phragmoplast architecture
creator: Renuka Kolli
description: . New microtubules are formed by a process called nucleation. In plants, nucleation occurs primarily on the walls of existing microtubules such that the nascent microtubules appear branched at particular angles. Many microtubule-associated proteins regulate microtubule dynamics by nucleation, stabilization, destabilization, capping, or cross-linking.

title: Evidence for long-standing mild-effect mutator alleles shaping genetic variation in S. cerevisiae populations
creator: Pengyao Jiang, Vidha Sudhesh, Megan My-Ngan Phan, Ishan Bansal, Cian Wheeler, Alan J Herr, Maitreya J. Dunham, Kelley Harris
description: Most mutations are neutral or deleterious, and mutator alleles that substantially increase the mutation rate of an organism are believed to be short-lived in natural populations. Theory suggests that mutator alleles of modest effect have the potential to segregate nearly neutrally, but this prediction has been difficult to test experimentally.

title: Fibrotic liver injury in biliary atresia: long-term implications
creator: Maria Hukkinen, Mikko P Pakarinen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Normalization of serum bilirubin after Kasai portoenterostomy (KPE) is a prerequisite for long-term native liver (NL) survival. Following a successful KPE, fibrotic liver injury progresses variably, although a significant proportion of patients show decreasing histological liver fibrosis during follow-up. Eventually, the great majority of patients develop cirrhosis and clinical manifestations of portal hypertension (PH), while liver malignancies and pulmonary complications of PH occur infrequently. Accurate prediction of liver fibrosis remains challenging.

title: Willingness-to-pay for community-based health insurance among formal and informal doctors in Dhaka, Bangladesh: a comparative cross-sectional study
creator: Md Fuad Al Fidah, Syeda Sumaiya Efa, Md Ziaul Islam
description: IntroductionHealth insurance enables financial protection and reduces medical burdens. Currently, less than 1% of Bangladeshi citizens have health insurance coverage. We aimed to assess the willingness-to-pay for community-based health insurance and explore associated factors among formal and informal doctors in Bangladesh.MethodsThis comparative cross-sectional study was conducted on Bangladeshi doctors with formal and informal employment.

title: Non-Covalent Poly(ADP-ribose) Signaling Organizes a Circadian E3 Ligase Network in the Brain
creator: Sajiv Harikrishnan, Sung-Ung Kang
description: Although PAR biology has traditionally been studied through covalent PARylation, non-covalent PAR-binding proteins provide an additional mechanism for interpreting transient PAR signals and converting them into downstream regulatory programs. Among these effectors, E3 ubiquitin ligases are uniquely positioned to couple PAR sensing to selective ubiquitination, thereby integrating stress signaling with proteostatic control.

title: Exploring the Synergistic Effects of Erinacines on Microglial Regulation and Alzheimer's Pathology Under Metabolic Stress
creator: Van Thanh Bui, Kuan‐Wei Wu, Chin‐Chu Chen, Anh Thuc Nguyen, Wei‐Jan Huang, Li‐Ya Lee, Wan‐Ping Chen, Chi‐Ying Huang, Young‐Ji Shiao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background Hericium erinaceus mycelium and its constituents, erinacines A and S, have shown neuroprotective effects in APP/PS1 transgenic mice; however, the precise mechanisms by which they modulate microglial phenotypes remain unclear. Our study is the first to explore the effect of erinacines on microglia morphology and the underlying mechanisms using a novel primary mixed glia cell model and advanced bioinformatic tools.

title: SE‐lncRNAs in Cancer: Classification, Subcellular Localisation, Function and Corresponding TFs
creator: Yuxin Bao, Songling Teng, Hanjie Zhai, Yuanzhuang Zhang, Yeqiu Xu, Chenghao Li, Zhenjun Chen, Fu Ren, Yong Wang

These lncRNAs, known as SE‐lncRNAs, are strongly linked to cancer and regulate cancer progression through multiple interactions with downstream targets. The expression of SE‐lncRNAs is controlled by various transcription factors (TFs), and dysregulation of these TFs can contribute to cancer development.

title: AthRiboNC: an Arabidopsis database for ncRNAs with coding potential revealed from ribosome profiling

description: c for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA), randomizing 178 patients with this relatively rare cancer type (1). This is an impressive and clinically important achievement in light of previous trials that have included patients with BTCs arising in the gallbladder, intra-/extrahepatic bile ducts, and ampulla of Vater (2,3), despite significant biological differences between these diseases (4).

title: Development and Application of Tumor Organoids: An Emerging Platform for Gynecological Cancers
creator: Yu Hu, Wei Chen, Xiaojing Zhang, Ying Wu, Furong Du, Jingrui Wang, Meijun He, Wei Sun
description: Gynecological cancers pose great health threats to women, in which ovarian cancer (OC), cervical cancer (CC) and endometrial cancer (EC) are most common. Conventional treatment modalities for gynecological cancers, such as surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy, are usually affected by multiple factors like drug resistance and recurrence.

title: Ceramide and C1P: a lipid love story of Brassica-Sclerotinia interaction
creator: Ritu Singh, Prem Pratap Singh
description: ks (Liu et al. 2021). Ceramides are central bioactive molecules in sphingolipid metabolism that influence fundamental processes such as cell differentiation, apoptosis, and immune regulation across eukaryotic systems. In plants, ceramides and their phosphorylated derivatives, ceramide-1-phosphate (C1P), play dual roles in programmed cell death (PCD), a key defense strategy against pathogens (DeMell et al. 2023).

title: Immune Checkpoint-Related Gene Polymorphisms and High Serum Concentration of PD-L1 and CTLA4 Contribute to the Resistance to Platinum-Based Chemotherapy in Cervical Cancer
creator: Hongqin Yuan, Xinfeng Wang, Kaidong Liu, Jia Zhang, Pei Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). PurposeThis study aims to evaluate the feasibility of using immune checkpoint-related gene polymorphisms and serum levels of PD-1, PD-L1 and CTLA4 in predicting chemotherapy resistance in patients with cervical cancer.MethodsSeven candidate SNPs in PDCD1, CD274 and CTLA4 were genotyped in 1032 cervical cancer patients (537 non-responders and 495 responders based on their responses to chemotherapy), and the serum level of PD-1, PD-L1 and CTLA4 was detected by ELISA.ResultsThe frequencies of minor allele A of PDCD1- rs2227982, CD274-rs2890658 and CTLA4-rs3087243 were significantly higher

title: Editorial for PREOPANC-2, a multicenter, open-label, phase 3 randomized trial comparing neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX vs. neoadjuvant gemcitabine based chemoradiotherapy in resectable and borderline resectable pancreatic cancer
creator: Chunjie Li, Kian-Huat Lim
description: ic cancer or borderline resectable pancreatic cancer (RPC, BRPC) disease. Due to the high propensity for early or occult metastasis, the complexity of PC surgery, and challenges in delivering adjuvant chemotherapy at the intended dose and schedule following surgery, there has been a shift over the past decade toward administering neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) for these patients.

title: Coevolution and Adaptation of Transition Nuclear Proteins and Protamines in Naturally Ascrotal Mammals Support the Black Queen Hypothesis
creator: Simin Chai, Jieqiong Kang, Tianzhen Wu, Yu Zheng, Xu Zhou, Shixia Xu, Wenhua Ren, Guang Yang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Protamines (PRMs) and transition nuclear proteins (TNPs) are two key classes of sperm nuclear basic proteins that regulate chromatin reorganization and condensation in the spermatozoon head, playing crucial roles in mammalian spermatogenesis. In scrotal mammals, such as humans, cryptorchidism, the failure of the testes to descend into the scrotal sac is generally associated with higher rates of defective spermatozoon quality and function. However, ascrotal mammals, such as cetaceans, with naturally undescended testes, produce normal spermatozoa similar to their scrotal counterparts.

title: The Effects of Obesity on Lung Physiology, the Prevalence and Severity of Chronic Pulmonary Diseases, and Inhalation Treatment
creator: Eleonore Fröhlich
description: Obesity itself induces macroscopic, microscopic, and functional changes in the lungs, potentially making obese individuals more susceptible to acute and chronic pulmonary diseases. Apart from direct contribution to the course of the disease, obesity-induced alterations of the respiratory tract may influence the delivery and efficacy of inhaled formulations.

title: Air-Test for prediction of postoperative pulmonary complications after general anaesthesia: promise, performance and limitations
creator: Kate Gallagher, Itay Bentov
description: Early identification of patients who are at risk can lead to interventions that would reduce this burden or may lead to better allocation of postoperative resources (5). ARISCAT remains the best-established PPC risk score (2,6). External validation in the PERISCOPE study showed generally good discriminative performance, although calibration varied across geographic regions and specialised populations (2,6).

title: A 5-Month-Old Infant With a Complicated Holiday Souvenir
creator: Iris Voogd, Sanne A (S ) E Kooistra, Jamie A van der Meer, Soëba Ehsary, Clementien Vermont, Els van Nood, Marjolijn S W Quaak, Anthony Amoroso, Priya Nori, David J Riedel
description: remarkable. He had been adequately vaccinated for his age. The travel history included a visit to Morocco at the age of 2 months. Prior to presentation in our hospital, empirical sepsis treatment was initiated. However, blood cultures were negative and the child remained febrile after 48 hours of antibiotic treatment.

title: Predictive Modeling of the Risk of Hyperglycemia in Psoriasis Patients Using Machine Learning: A Multicenter Retrospective Study
creator: Mengyan Hu, Dingyuan Chen, Jian Yu
description: PurposeThis study aims to develop and validate machine learning models for predicting hyperglycemia risk in psoriasis patients.MethodsClinical data from 575 psoriasis patients admitted to the Department of Dermatology were collected and randomly split into a training set and an internal test set in a 7:3 ratio.

title: Beyond biochemical recovery: rethinking liver dysfunction in Kawasaki disease
creator: Yoshitaka Watanabe, Hirokazu Ikeda
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). y is uncommon in most patients (1,2). Contrarily, the main clinical concern in KD remains coronary artery involvement, as coronary abnormalities determine long-term cardiovascular risk and represent the primary target of established treatment strategies (3). This difference in prognostic importance creates fundamental uncertainty regarding hepatic involvement: should liver dysfunction be regarded as a condition requiring specific treatment or is it mainly a biochemical manifestation of systemic inflammation that improves with appropriate KD management? In the current issue, Wang et al.

title: Advancements in Molecular Diagnosis and Pharmacotherapeutic Strategies for Invasive Pituitary Adenomas
creator: Dingkai Xu, Ling Wang, Maohua Zheng
description: BackgroundThe overwhelming majority of pituitary tumors consist of pituitary adenomas (PAs), which have recently also been termed pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs). Clinically significant PAs occur in approximately one in every 1000 individuals, while other types of pituitary tumors, such as craniopharyngiomas and pituicytomas, are significantly less common. Although PAs are generally benign, a subset of them exhibits malignant‐like biological traits.

title: A rare case report: atypical presentation of Klinefelter syndrome in a 24-year-old male at suburban tertiary care hospital in Nepal
creator: Bhawana Bastola, Barada Bajracharya, Abhyuday Kumar Yadav, Rajendra Tamrakar
description: Klinefelter syndrome (KS) is the most common chromosomal condition affecting males, usually caused by the presence of an extra X chromosome (47, XXY). However, it often remains undiagnosed until adulthood. We report a unique case of a 24-year-old man whose primary concern was persistent nausea and vomiting, an atypical presenting complaint of Klinefelter syndrome.

title: Considerations for Glaucoma Evaluation and Management in Refractive Surgery Candidates
creator: Kasem Seresirikachorn, Angela Y Zhu, Ta Chen Chang
description: The popularity of refractive surgery has grown significantly in recent years, yet concerns about its effects on glaucoma evaluation and progression remain unclear. Various techniques in both corneal and lens-based refractive surgery have been developed, necessitating different strategies for monitoring glaucoma.

title: Mentalizing About Dynamic Social Action Sequences Is Supported by the Cerebellum, Basal Ganglia, and Neocortex: A Meta‐Analysis of Activation and Connectivity
creator: Frank Van Overwalle, Elien Heleven, Naem Haihambo, Meijia Li, Qianying Ma, Min Pu, Chris Baeken, Natacha Deroost, Kris Baetens
description: The posterior cerebellum and anterior basal ganglia are critical subcortical structures for learning and identifying dynamic action sequences, in concert with the neocortex. The present analysis investigates the role of action sequences during social mentalizing, termed here dynamic or sequential social mentalizing.

title: Improving the Quality of Lateral Wrist Radiographs: A Closed-Loop Audit of Radiographic Compliance With Standard Positioning Criteria
creator: Kunjan Barot, Adam khan Rahim, Izza Afzal, Hassan Imtiaz, Georgios Kouklidis, Talha Ahmed, Atizaz A Jan, Abdullah Durrani, Rizwana Monzur, John Lynch
description: BackgroundWrist injuries represent a substantial proportion of acute musculoskeletal presentations, with distal radius and carpal fractures among the most frequently encountered upper-limb fractures in emergency and orthopaedic services. Accurate lateral wrist radiographs are essential for detecting osseous and carpal alignment abnormalities, guiding management, and preventing complications. However, radiographic quality is highly dependent on adherence to established positioning standards.

title: The urinary pathobiont Actinobaculum massiliense can generate androgens via the dirAB pathway
creator: Taojun Wang, Saeed Ahmad, Raissa Santos de Lima Rosa, Briawna Binion, Francelys V. Fernandez-Materan, Jimoh Olamilekan Igbalaye, David Chung, Anika Bushra, Vince Perez, Michael A. Biedak, Elizabeth Tang, Betsy Barnick, Damie Olukoya, Pauline Mbuvi, Debapriya Dutta, John W. Erdman, H. Rex Gaskins, Gl
description: While overlooked during the Human Microbiome Project, characterizing the urinary microbiota in health and disease is a new frontier in microbiome science. Recent studies have associated differential abundance of bacterial taxa including Propionimicrobium lymphophilum and Actinobaculum/Actinotignum spp. with prostate cancer.

title: Hypophosphatemia after CAR-T cell therapy: a prospective study of inflammation, tubular injury and phosphate handling
creator: Francesc Moncho-Francés, Rafael Hernani, Miguel Angel Solis-Salguero, Ana Benzaquén, Isabel Juan-García, Ariadna Pérez-Martínez, Mireia Micó, Juan F Navarro-González, Jose Luis Piñana, Juan Carlos Hernández Boluda, María Jose Terol, Carlos Solano, Jose Luis Górriz, Isidro Torregrosa
description: BackgroundHypophosphatemia is a frequent electrolyte abnormality after chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy, but the clinical and biological factors associated with phosphate decline remain poorly defined. We prospectively evaluated the incidence, determinants, and potential biological associations of hypophosphatemia after CAR-T therapy.

title: Rheumatic Heart Disease Education Tools Integrated Into a Screening Program in Brazil: Acceptability and Knowledge Gain
creator: Jessica Abrams, Wanessa C Vinhal, Craig A Sable, Clareci S Cardoso, Liesl Zühlke, Alison Spaziani, Laylah Ryklief, Maria Carmo P Nunes, Isabely Karoline S Ribeiro, Rebeca Previero, Lorena R Silva, Luz M Tacuri Chavez, Kaciane K B Oliveira, Ingred Beatriz Amaral, Larissa Lemos, Julliane S Correa, Cec
description: Background:Rheumatic heart disease (RHD) is a preventable cause of premature death among young individuals in low- and middle-income countries. Education is a key strategy to alleviate the burden of this disease. We aimed to assess the acceptability and knowledge gain of a series of low-literacy education flipcharts, presented during screening in high-burden areas of Brazil.

title: Chlamydia Abortus-Induced Pneumonia with Psychiatric Symptoms and Pneumomediastinum: A Case Report
creator: Bing Ding, Zengkai Xu, Youtang Li, Zhiyi Ma
description: BackgroundChlamydia abortus is a zoonotic pathogen that commonly causes abortion, pelvic inflammatory disease, or septicemia during pregnancy in humans. It can occasionally lead to pneumonia.Case PresentationWe report a 35-year-old male with pneumonia complicated by psychiatric symptoms and pneumomediastinum. Initial treatment with cefotaxime and piperacillin-tazobactam failed. On admission, chest CT revealed bilateral pulmonary inflammation, pneumomediastinum, and cervical subcutaneous emphysema.

title: Relationship Between Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction and ICD‐10 Codes Among Patients Hospitalized With Heart Failure
creator: Ty J. Gluckman, Shih‐Ting Chiu, Deanna Rider, Phil K. Tseng, James O. Mudd, Joshua D. Remick, Craig Granowitz, Amy Carroll, Slaven Sikirica, Mario E. Canonico, Judith Hsia, Marc P. Bonaca
description: IntroductionWhile left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) represents an important means by which to classify patients with heart failure (HF), relatively little is known about the distribution of LVEFs among patients hospitalized for HF based on their International Classification of Disease (ICD)‐10 code.

title: Synthesis, structure and computational study of di­acetato­bis­(2-amino-6-fluoro-1,3-benzo­thia­zole-κN3)zinc(II)
creator: Dilshoda Amanova, Zubaydabegim Radjabova, Sardor Murodov, Sevinch Erkinboyeva, Odil Choriev, Jamshid Ashurov, Shahlo Daminova
description: The title tetra­hedral ZnII complex with 2-amino-6-fluoro-1,3-benzo­thia­zole has been structurally characterized. The crystal packing is consolidated by N—H⋯O, bifurcated N—H⋯(O,F), C—H⋯π, O⋯π and offset π–π inter­actions. Chemical context Benzo­thia­zole derivatives constitute an important class of nitro­gen- and sulfur-containing heterocyclic compounds owing to their structural diversity, coordination versatility and broad spectrum of biological and physicochemical properties (Keri et al., 2015 ▸).

title: Potential Arrival Pathway for Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza H5N1 to Oceania
creator: Pablo Plaza, Andrea Santangeli, Tommaso Cancellario, Sergio Lambertucci
description: ns such as the Americas and Antarctica for the first time in its evolutionary history [3]. However, no cases of H5N1 have been detected in Oceania to date [5, 6] (only one human case infected outside this continent has been reported [7]).

title: Synthesis and structure of ethyl 2,2-dimethyl-3-(naphthalen-1-yl)-1,2-di­hydro­benzo[c]siline-4-carboxyl­ate
creator: Xiaoxiao Tang, Liyun Zhang
description: In the title compound, C24H24O2Si, the ethyl ester substituent shows two-site disorder and C—H⋯O contacts generate zigzag ribbons extending along [010]. Chemical context Silacyclic fused skeletons represent appealing building blocks for synthetic chemistry, optoelectronic materials and medicinal chemistry (Bains et al., 2003 ▸; Ikeno et al., 2017 ▸; Fujii et al., 2017 ▸).

title: Pain Relief During Cystoscopic Ureteral Stent Extraction by Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation: A Double-Blinded, Randomized, Controlled Trial
creator: Qiaoling Chen, Huidan Lian, Junlu Wang, Lili Chen, Ruolin Shi, Meizi Qian
description: BackgroundAcupuncture has pain-relief effects, but no data are available on transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS) for pain relief during transurethral removal of ureteral stents. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of TEAS in reducing pain during cystoscopic ureteral stent extraction.

title: Comparative evaluation of 2D and 3D YouTube videos as supplementary educational resources for vitreoretinal surgery training
creator: Zubeyir Yozgat, Halime Kubra Sahin, Gizem Ilayda Dumlupinar, Mehmet Cem Sabaner
description: Ophthalmologists and ophthalmology residents (ORs) are increasingly turning to the internet for medical information, underscoring the significant role that YouTube videos, particularly three-dimensional (3D) ones, play in lifelong learning. This study aimed to compare the content and quality of 3D YouTube videos with two-dimensional (2D) videos as supplementary educational tools for vitreoretinal surgery.

title: Timing of Endotracheal Intubation After High-Flow Nasal Cannula Initiation in Patients With Mild-to-Moderate Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study
creator: Niki Pavlatou, Maria Polikandrioti, Evgenia Stergiopoulou, Georgia Toulia, Antonia Kalogianni
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) is widely used in acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, including mild-to-moderate acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Some patients deteriorate and require invasive mechanical ventilation, but the appropriate timing of intubation remains uncertain. This study examined the association between intubation within 24 hours of HFNC initiation and clinical outcomes among patients with mild-to-moderate ARDS in whom HFNC failed.Methods: This prospective observational cohort included 109 adults with mild-to-moderate ARDS treated at the General Hospital of Athens "G.

title: The Impact of the Core-Shell Fiber Composition on the Properties and Stability of the Electrospun Films
creator: Ewelina Łyszczarz, Aleksandra Rezka, Dorota Majda, Witold Jamróz, Aleksander Mendyk
description: PurposeThis study aimed to develop and evaluate core–shell electrospun orodispersible films (ODFs) containing lopinavir (LPV) and ritonavir (RTV) for pediatric HIV therapy. The investigation focused on the impact of fiber composition and storage conditions on film morphology, physicochemical stability, mechanical properties, disintegration time, and drug dissolution profiles.

title: Laboratory biosafety: A visual analysis in the web of science database from 2000 to 2022: A review
creator: Sunyun Qi, Siyuan Chen, Dries De Witte, Geert Molenberghs, Qifeng Zhang, Hua Gu, Yanchao Gao
description: To conduct a visual analysis of institutional publications, individual publications and publication keywords in the field of laboratory biosafety using the Web of Science database from 2000 to 2022.VOSviewer 1.6.18 was used to study the relation between paper authors, and CiteSpace 6.1.R6 was used to visualize the collaboration between the paper institutions, the paper keywords and the timeline.

title: Unusual Root Canal Morphology in Mandibular Molars: A Case Series
creator: Shelja Mohan, Arjama Chaudhury, George Thomas, Sunil Jose, Sibi Aboobacker
description: The complex root canal anatomy of mandibular molars often poses a challenge for endodontic treatment. To overcome this, precise access, cleaning, shaping, and three-dimensional obturation are essential. This case report presents three unusual cases of mandibular molars, where rare root canal configurations were accurately diagnosed using cone beam computed tomography (CBCT), and sonic activation was used for disinfection.

title: Sense of Coherence: factorial structure and association with oral health - a study of Norwegian adults
creator: Victoria Xenaki, Anne Nordrehaug Åstrøm
description: ObjectiveAssess the construct validity of Sense of Coherence (SOC) by testing a one- and a three-factor structure and associations with oral health indicators.MethodIn all, 9000 adults were randomly selected from a national population panel of 83,000 and 1,557 completed telephone interviews. SOC was measured using the 13-item Norwegian version of the original 29-item Orientation to Life questionnaire.

title: High-resolution structures of human NHE6 and NHE9 elucidate endosomal ion and lipid interactions
creator: Jesper S. Hansen, Ashley C. W. Pike, Gamma Chi, Gernot Wolf, Jeppe Tranberg-Jensen, Hannah Lichtmannegger, David Speedman, Alvaro Ingles-Prieto, Fabian Goericke, Helena Batoulis, Hartmut Beck, Rajini Rao, Tooraj Mirshahi, David B. Sauer, Giulio Superti-Furga, Kilian V. M. Huber
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Endosomal NHE6 (SLC9A6) and NHE9 (SLC9A9) transporters are essential for maintaining pH homeostasis within endosomes and their dysfunction has been linked to neurological and neurodegenerative disorders. NHE6 and NHE9 are widely considered to function as electroneutral exchangers that couple the export of protons to the import of sodium or potassium ions across cellular membranes, thereby forming the basis of proton leak pathways for internal pH balancing and fine-tuning.

title: Autoimmune Psychosis Exists: Early Diagnosis of an Anti‐NMDA Receptor Autoimmune Encephalitis Presenting as First‐Episode Psychosis in a 25‐Year‐Old Male—A Case Report
creator: Marc Mourad, Caroline Hallal, Juliana Sargi, Elie Atallah, Anthony Kassab, Sajida Sabsaby, Christian Matta, Karine Abou Khaled, Sami Richa
description: BackgroundAnti‐N‐methyl‐D‐aspartate receptor (NMDAR) encephalitis is an autoimmune disorder marked by prominent neuropsychiatric symptoms. It is typically first encountered by psychiatrists because psychotic symptoms can be early signs of the condition. In recent years, this form of encephalitis has been established as a distinct diagnostic entity in neurology and psychiatry.

title: The effectiveness of care robots in alleviating physical burden and pain for caregivers: Non-randomized prospective interventional study – Preliminary study
creator: Jae Ik Jung, Yoo Seok Jeong, Dong Rak Kwon
description: Background:Caregiver burden significantly affects both patients and caregivers but is often overlooked in clinical practice. Physical and emotional strain on caregivers can compromise the quality of care. Care robots are emerging as solutions to alleviate these burdens by assisting with routine tasks, thereby reducing caregivers’ physical strain and stress.

title: Various Antihypertensive Drug Compliance Models and Cardiovascular Prognosis of People With Incidentally Detected High Blood Pressure During Health Check‐Up in Korea
creator: Jong-Kwan Park, Sungyoun Chun, Joongmin Kim, Hancheol Lee, Ji-Yong Jang, Kyeong-Hyeon Chun, Hyeongsoo Kim, Seung-Jin Oh, Geunhee Park, Se-Jung Yoon
description: BackgroundA health check‐up system (HCS) is one of the best ways to prevent complications and maintain health by diagnosing diseases and screening risk factors early. Here, we investigated how many people who detected elevated blood pressure through the HCS were finally diagnosed with “hypertension” and continuously treated.

title: Reproducible human reward imaging phenotypes exhibit differential sensitivity to dopamine D2 receptor antagonism
creator: Nicola Sambuco, Antonella Lupo, Peter C. T. Hawkins, Pierluigi Selvaggi, Linda A. Antonucci, Alessandro Bertolino, Giuseppe Blasi, Piergiuseppe Di Palo, Luigi Grassi, Daniela Grasso, Philipp Homan, Gian Marco Leggio, Francesco Massari, Alessio Maria Monteleone, Martin Osugo, Roberta Passiatore, Ales
description: Human reward processing varies along cue-centric and outcome-centric axes, but the mechanistic basis of individual variation in incentive salience attribution remains incompletely characterized. Here we show, using fMRI across five cohorts (N-total = 1251; N1 = 890; N2 = 245; N3 = 34; N4 = 48; N5 = 34), two reproducible imaging phenotypes mirroring sign- and goal-tracking (ST-like, GT-like).

title: Predictors of active and recurrent bleeding in upper gastrointestinal angiodysplasia: Results from 10-year esophagogastroduodenoscopy of a tertiary center in Taiwan
creator: Meng-Chuan Lu, Tien-Yu Huang, Peng-Jen Chen, Hsuan-Wei Chen, Chih-Wei Yang, Jung-Chun Lin, Wei-Chen Huang, Hsuan-Hwai Lin, Yu-Lueng Shih, Tsai-Yuan Hsieh, Bao-Chung Chen
description: Upper gastrointestinal angiodysplasia (UGIA) is a unique mucosal vascular lesion that causes acute or recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding. Despite the increasing incidence of UGIA, the risk factors for bleeding in this condition remain unclear. We investigated the predictors of active and recurrent bleeding among patients with UGIA.

title: Gestational Diabetes Is Associated With Abnormalities in Glucose Excursion in Early Pregnancy
creator: Salwa Al-Maraghi, Safa Alzneika, Dhowa Al-Ali, Fatma Al-Haddad, Aly Mostafa Hassan, Sara Al-Thani, Noora Al-Khalaf, Farhan Cyprian, Mohamed Iheb Bougmiza, Bushra Nadeem, Hanan Khudadad, Stephen Beer, Mohammed Bashir, Abdul-Badi Abou-Samra, Suhail A. R. Doi
description: AimsIt is unknown if dysglycemia at 24–28 weeks of pregnancy is preceded by glycemic changes earlier in pregnancy. This study therefore examines the association between glucose excursion in the first 20 gestational weeks and the onset of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) in the early third trimester.

title: Indirect Single-Step Apexification Utilizing a Carrier-Supported Custom-Fit Biomaterial: A Novel Technique Using Mineral Trioxide Aggregate and Biodentine
creator: Damini Kesarwani, Sunandan Mittal, Vanita Keshav, Tarun Kumar
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Management of teeth with open apices remains technically challenging because conventional apexification techniques may be associated with prolonged treatment, multiple clinical visits, difficulty in controlling apical barrier placement, and the risk of extrusion of biomaterial beyond the apical foramen.

title: Predictive Value of Pyroptosis Markers (NLRP3, HMGB1, and Caspase‐1) in the Prognosis of Patients With Metastatic Breast Cancer: A Prospective Observational Study
creator: Yi Zhang, Ying He, Qiang Liu, Hongwu Deng
description: ObjectiveThe predictive value of serum pyroptosis markers, including NOD‐like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3), high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), and caspase‐1, in metastatic breast cancer (MBC) patients was investigated.MethodsA prospective observational study was conducted, enrolling MBC patients who had not undergone prior radiotherapy or chemotherapy.

title: Patient-Reported Barriers to Mammography Screening Among Women at a Community Health Clinic in Southeastern Michigan: A Cross-Sectional Pilot Study
creator: Miranda Goodson, Karen Abdelmalek, Dina Bayachou, Rhea Sehgal, Dea Kanani, Whitney Bowyer, Alexis Kralovich, Anna Lundh, Sarah Qureshi, Nina Agemy, Laura J Benjamins
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: The objective of this cross-sectional pilot study was to explore patient-reported barriers to mammography screening and women's knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors regarding mammography among women receiving care at a university-affiliated community health clinic in Southeastern Michigan (SEM).Methods: A 47-item investigator-developed exploratory questionnaire informed by the Health Belief Model (HBM) constructs was distributed via Qualtrics from August to December 2025 to women receiving care at a local community health clinic.

title: Experimental studies of the effects of hydrophobic coatings on flow separation around 3D bluff bodies
creator: Naseeb Ahmed Siddiqui, Martin Agelin-Chaab
description: This study explores how hydrophobic coating influences the structure of the flow separation at the rear end of 3D bluff bodies. Two 3D representative bluff bodies, namely the standard Ahmed body (SAB), which features flow separation and reattachment at its slant surface, and the elliptical Ahmed body (EAB), which exhibits fully separated flow, are employed.

title: Open-source cell culture automation system with integrated cell counting for passaging microplate cultures
creator: Greg Courville, Shivanshi Vaid, Alexis Toruño, Paul Lebel, Joana P Cabrera, Preethi Raghavan, Axel Jacobsen, George R R Bell, Manuel D Leonetti, Rafael Gómez-Sjöberg
description: Tissue culture in 96-well microplates is conventionally a tedious, highly manual process sensitive to individual technique and experimenter error. Here, we describe the Automated Cell Culture Splitter, a system for passaging plates of adherent or suspension cells, for routine culture maintenance or specialized applications such as seeding plates for microscopy.

title: Bilateral Maxillary Fourth and Fifth Molars in a 17-Year-Old Female
creator: Hikari Wakao, Takahiro Takekawa, Karen Gomi, Akinori Moroi, Koichiro Ueki
description: Supernumerary teeth are relatively common in clinical practice; however, the occurrence of multiple supernumerary teeth in a bilaterally symmetrical pattern is rare. A 17-year-old female was referred to our department for extraction of impacted third molars. Panoramic radiography revealed two bilaterally symmetrical tooth-like structures adjacent to each maxillary third molar.

title: Femtosecond Laser Engraving Promotes the Repopulation of Decellularized Human Articular Cartilage
creator: Conny Schneider, Johann Zehetner, Barbara Schädl, Matthias Domke, Claudia Keibl, Bernhard Rieder, Patrick Heimel, Anne Kleiner, Andreas Teuschl-Woller, Susanne Wolbank, Heinz Redl, Sylvia Nürnberger
description: Decellularized articular cartilage of human origin presents itself as the most homologous filling material for focal cartilage defects. Yet, the full repopulation of the exceptionally dense collagen construct has never been achieved without providing host cells with artificially created migration paths into the matrix.

title: Serum pentraxin-3 as a potential biomarker for diagnosis and prognosis in primary liver cancer: An observational study
creator: Li Chen, Shifu Song, Mao Chen, Qin Liu, Hongchi Zhou
description: This study aimed to examine serum pentraxin 3 levels in patients with primary liver cancer and to assess its potential as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker. Serum samples were obtained from 180 patients with primary liver cancer and 180 healthy control subjects. The concentration of PTX3 in these samples was measured using an ELISA kit.

title: Acinetobacter baumannii Nosocomial Meningitis Secondary to Neurosurgical Intervention: A Case Report
creator: Inssaf Haddi, Yousra Boughalem, Youssef El Kamouni, Lamiae Arsalane, Said Zouhair
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Nosocomial meningitis is a serious complication of neurosurgical procedures, associated with high morbidity and mortality, as well as significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Among the causative pathogens, Acinetobacter baumannii (A. baumannii) is particularly concerning due to its ability to survive for prolonged periods in the hospital environment, its opportunistic virulence, and, especially, its tendency to develop multidrug resistance to antimicrobial agents.

title: Elevated Cathepsin B enzyme levels: a potential risk indicator for rheumatoid arthritis: Insights from a Mendelian randomization study
creator: Ruolin Hou, Xin Liu, Changzhen Zhang, Shuiqi Cai, Chengyi Liu, Qun Huang
description: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease that significantly impacts the quality of life of affected individuals. Observational data have consistently pointed towards an associative relationship between cathepsins and the development of RA. Nonetheless, the establishment of a definitive causal nexus between members of the cathepsin family and the pathogenesis of RA remains elusive.

title: Perda de altura radial em pacientes submetidos à fixação com placa bloqueada anatômica volar de rádio distal: Um estudo retrospectivo em uma instituição pública
creator: Heitor Teixeira Alves Carvalho, Yves Pacheco Dias March e Souza, Felipe Pinheiro da Silva, Érica Maciel Heringer, João Carlos Ostermeir Silva Pereira, Saulo Fontes de Almeida
description: ResumoObjetivoAvaliar e quantificar a frequência e magnitude da perda tardia de parâmetros radiográficos de redução de fraturas de rádio distal em pacientes operados com placa volar bloqueada.MétodosEste é um estudo retrospectivo e transversal que analisou radiograficamente 65 punhos operados entre 2020 e 2024 em uma instituição pública, avaliando a perda de altura radial no seguimento pós-operatório.

title: Causal effects of the RANK-RANKL-OPG system and scoliosis: A bidirectional 2-sample Mendelian randomization study
creator: Wei Xie, Wen-Tao Wan, Shuai-Yi Liu, Jia-Qi Wang, Chao Chen, Xun Sun, Xin-Yu Liu, Qiang Yang
description: Epidemiological studies and a recent Mendelian randomization (MR) study have identified an association between low bone mass and an increased risk of scoliosis. Previous research suggests that bone loss in patients with scoliosis may be related to the RANK-RANKL-OPG system. This study is to investigate whether a causal relationship exists between the RANK-RANKL-OPG system and the development of scoliosis.

title: Systemic treatment paradigms for unresectable and advanced hepatocellular carcinoma in Europe
creator: David J Pinato, Eleonora Alimenti, Pasquale Lombardi, Juan Vaz, Antonia Digklia, Julien Edeline, Najib Ben Khaled, Emanuela Di Giacomo, Bernhard Scheiner, Jose Presa Ramos, Grainne M O’Kane, Sarah Cappuyns, Giulia Tesini, Lorenza Rimassa
description: SummaryThe management of unresectable and advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has been transformed by the introduction of immune checkpoint inhibitor-based combinations, which have improved response and survival and expanded first-line treatment options. The availability of multiple effective regimens has introduced new challenges in therapeutic decision making.

title: Xuebijing and somatostatin against acute pancreatitis: A systematic review and network pharmacology
creator: Ji-Ping Cao, Xiang-Hua Piao, Long-Xun Zhu, Pan-Feng Feng
description: Background:Acute pancreatitis (AP) is a common pancreatic disease. Xuebijing injection (XBJ) combined with somatostatin in the treatment of AP is frequently used in clinical practice. There is, however, a lack of high-quality evidence-based evidence and network pharmacology to regard the therapeutic efficacy and pharmacological mechanisms.

title: Distinct gut microbial profile in PIT1 lineage PitNETs: a potential link to cognitive impairment
creator: Junjun Li, Lingye Zhang, Chen Ma, Jiang Long, Jinpeng Lv, Xingli Deng
description: BackgroundPatients with pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs) frequently experience cognitive impairment (CI), yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood.MethodIn this study, we assessed cognitive function in 42 PitNETs patients and 42 healthy controls using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), evaluating the effects of tumor volume, invasiveness, pituitary hormone levels, lineage, and surgical intervention.

title: Evolving aspects of oral care in older adults: a systematic review and Meta-synthesis
creator: Arash Neshati, Noosha Farzaie Ardejanie, Samaneh Naeimi, Marzieh Pashmforosh, Zahra Askari, Alireza Rafi
description: BackgroundThe global aging population has heightened the need for comprehensive oral care in older adults, yet evolving aspects such as preventive strategies, technological advancements, and interdisciplinary approaches remain underexplored. This systematic review and qualitative meta-synthesis aimed to synthesize qualitative evidence on perceptions, experiences, barriers, facilitators, and impacts of oral care in older adults, guided by the Socio-Ecological Model.

title: Upregulation of miR-502-5p in traumatic spinal cord injury modulates neuroinflammation and oxidative stress by targeting FBXO28
creator: Di Qiu, Juanyu Liu, Xintong Hao, Jinxiang Zhang
description: BackgroundSpinal cord injury (SCI) is a serious condition affecting the central nervous system, often caused by trauma, which can lead to lasting impairment in nerve function.ObjectiveThis study aims to explore the functional role of miR-502-5p in traumatic SCI, offering insights into potential therapeutic interventions.

title: The mediating role of the genetically predicted N6, N6, N6-trimethyllysine levels in the association between HLA DR on CD14‐ CD16+ monocytes and ankylosing spondylitis
creator: Danyun Hua, Lu Wang, Na Li, Xiang Xu, Xiaohu Yin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This study explores the hidden connection between HLA DR on CD14‐ CD16+ monocytes and ankylosing spondylitis (AS), with a particular emphasis on investigating and measuring the impact of 1091 blood metabolites as potential mediators. We harnessed the power of summary-level data extracted from a comprehensive genome-wide association study to delve into the intricate relationship between genetically predicted HLA DR on CD14‐ CD16+ monocytes (3621 cases) and AS (1193 cases and 374,621 controls).

title: Effectiveness of transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation for lower limb rehabilitation in spinal cord injury: a systematic review
creator: Ravi Shankar, Kevin Sim Wei Wen, Ziyu Goh, Brandon Tan, Gobinathan Chandran
description: BackgroundSpinal cord injury (SCI) results in devastating motor and sensory deficits below the level of injury. Transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation (tSCS) has emerged as a promising non-invasive neuromodulation technique for improving motor function in individuals with SCI. However, the effectiveness of tSCS for lower limb rehabilitation remains unclear.

title: TSPO PET selectively detects the denervated skeletal muscle district remodeling after experimental peripheral nerve injury
creator: Serena Losacco, Irene Di Patrizi, Edoardo Dighero, Maddalena Ghelardoni, Mattia Riondato, Roberta Resaz, Laura Emionite, Sabrina Chiesa, Matteo Bauckneht, Mattia Camera, Giovanna Capodivento, Francesca Vitale, Sonia Carta, Luca Sofia, Roberta Piva, Anna Maria Orengo, Mehrnaz Hamedani, Federico Zaott
description: BackgroundPeripheral nerve injury induces inflammatory and stress-related remodeling in downstream skeletal muscle before overt atrophy develops, yet non-invasive approaches capable of detecting and anatomically localizing early muscle involvement remain limited. The 18-kDa translocator protein (TSPO), a marker of inflammatory activation and mitochondrial stress, is a molecular target for PET imaging with [1⁸F]DPA-714.

title: Renal cell carcinoma and macrophage research: A bibliometric analysis (2004–2023)
creator: Dingtian Qi, Haoxun Zhang, Feng Xiong, Guoling Zhang, Boju Tao, Chunyang Wang
description: To analyze hotspots and trends in renal cell carcinoma (RCC)-macrophage research using bibliometric analysis, although numerous studies on macrophages in RCC have been recently reported, understanding the progressive trends in this field remains challenging. Publications focused on macrophages in RCC were extracted from the Web of Science Core Collection.

title: PEGylated Positively Charged Fluorescent Silica Nanoparticles for Enhanced Gene Delivery in Canola (Brassica napus)
creator: Zhila Osmani, Muhammad Amirul Islam, Lipu Wang, Rui Wen, Wei Xiao, Guanqun Chen, Marianna Kulka
description: Genetic transformation of Brassica napus (canola) using conventional methods remains limited by low efficiency and tissue-specific barriers, but nanoparticle (NP)-mediated delivery offers a promising complementary approach to overcome these limitations. In this study, a PEGylated, positively charged fluorescent silica nanoparticle (SiO2NP–TMAC/FITC/PEG) was developed and evaluated for DNA delivery and real-time tracking in canola protoplasts and microspores.

title: Beyond Anticoagulation: Limitations of Oral Anticoagulants in Preventing Stroke Recurrence in Atrial Fibrillation
creator: Jessica Seetge, Balázs Cséke, Zsófia Nozomi Karádi, Edit Bosnyák, László Szapáry, Umberto Aguglia
description: Background/Objectives: Despite the widespread use of oral anticoagulants (OACs), acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains a significant risk for patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). The real-world effectiveness of OACs in preventing recurrent strokes, particularly following an initial stroke of cardioembolic (CE) origin, continues to be a major challenge for clinicians managing AF patients.

title: Comparison of the TyG index, TyG-traditional obesity indices, and TyG-novel obesity indices: does increased complexity help in predicting cardiometabolic multimorbidity?
creator: Fanzhi Zhang, Bin Zhang, Xinfang Huang, Zhenyu Wang, Juan Wang, Houhui Lan, Guobo Xie, Wei Wang, Yang Zou, Chao Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is an important determinant influencing the incidence of cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM). However, it remains unclear whether combining the TyG index with novel obesity indices (CVAI/BRI/ABSI/WWI) can improve the risk stratification of CMM.

title: Glycolytic Reprogramming Mediated by the OTUD4-FXR1-HIF1A Axis Drives Gastric Cancer Progression
creator: Fulin Wang, Yu Shao, Xiaomei Zhuang, Xiumin Liu, Yu Hu, Chen Dai, Jia Chen, Yong Kuang, Gangqiang Wang, Zhenzhen Zhao, Nan Cai, Liang Gu, Guoying Zhou, Hongwu Chu, Huimin Zhao, Cuncan Deng, Changhua Zhang
description: Ubiquitination and deubiquitination play critical roles in gastric cancer progression, yet systematic investigations of ubiquitin-regulating proteins in gastric cancer (GC) remain limited. To identify key regulators, we performed Ubiquitin-Focused CRISPR-Cas9 growth-based screening in GC cells and identified the deubiquitinase OTUD4 as a candidate gene promoting tumor growth.

title: Exploring the relationship between spiritual sensitivity and compassionate care among nurses: a cross-sectional study
creator: Majid Tavakol, Nahid Tavakol, Shohreh Javadpour
description: BackgroundCompassionate care is a fundamental ethical component of nursing that significantly influences patient outcomes, satisfaction, and healthcare provider well-being. Spiritual sensitivity, reflecting a nurse’s ability to recognize and respond empathetically to patients’ spiritual needs, is increasingly recognized as a key driver of compassionate care.

title: In Situ Ultrasonic Characterization of Hydrogen Damage Evolution in X80 Pipeline Steel
creator: Bing Chen, Feifei Qiu, Li Xia, Lintao Xu, Junjun Jin, Guoqing Gou
description: A nondestructive evaluation of the hydrogen damage of materials in a hydrogen environment is important for monitoring the running conditions of various pieces of equipment. In this work, a new thermostatic electrolytic hydrogenation in situ ultrasonic test system (In Situ TEH-UT) was developed.

title: Detection of Hydrogen Peroxide Vapors Using Acidified Titanium(IV)-Based Test Strips
creator: Rayhan Hossain, Nicholas F Materer, Bang-An Lu, Yuanhui Cheng
