creator: Alia Ali Galadari, Moteb Al Otaibi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Valsalva purpura refers to purpura resulting from performing the Valsalva maneuver, a forced expiratory effort against a closed glottis. There are limited reported cases of Valsalva purpura in children, specifically on the cheeks. We present the case of a 7-year-old child who developed Valsalva purpura on his cheeks after performing the Valsalva maneuver during deep breathing exercises by holding his breath underwater during his swimming sessions. This article overviews the relationship between the Valsalva maneuver, purpura, and similar cases.

title: Cardamonin mitigates kidney injury by modulating inflammation, oxidative stress, and apoptotic signaling in rats subjected to renal ischemia and reperfusion
creator: Haidar Hameed Ali Al-Sultany, Murooj Altimimi, Heider Qassam, Najah Rayish Hadi
description: Renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is a critical health concern that aggravates the pathophysiology of acute kidney injury (AKI), leading to high mortality rates in intensive care units. Cardamonin is a natural compound with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. The current study aimed to evaluate the renoprotective impact of cardamonin against AKI induced by renal IRI.

title: A compressive sensing-driven data collection scheme for UAV-assisted wireless sensor networks
creator: Zhe Han, Guoqiang Zheng, Chuanfeng Li, Guoqiang Wang, Yu Mu
description: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have demonstrated significant potential as mobile nodes for data collection in sensor networks. However, the environmental conditions in remote areas often fail to offer stable and reliable energy supply for energy-constrained UAVs and sensing nodes (SNs). Consequently, efficient energy utilization strategies is crucial for maintaining the long-term and stable operation of such networks.

title: Immediate and localized effect of Kinesio tape on the hand grip strength of sedentary female adults
creator: Mariam Ameer, Ammar Al Abbad, Arun Vijay Subbarayalu, Areej Alsharari, Rawan AlRuwaili, Saylah AlFuhigi, Nadia Hmdan, Amjad Alshammari, Ghala Alhuthayl
description: The current study aimed to assess the immediate and localized effect of Kinesio Taping (KT) on hand grip strength. A cross-sectional study was conducted on 60 sedentary female university students (aged 18-23) divided into two groups of 30 subjects each.

title: From U to mnm⁵Se²U: tuning base pairing preferences through 2-chalcogen and 5-methylaminomethyl modifications
creator: Paulina Kuwerska, Katarzyna Kulik, Karolina Podskoczyj, Agnieszka Dziergowska, Elzbieta Sochacka, Tomasz Bartosik, Malgorzata Sierant, Barbara Nawrot, Grazyna Leszczynska
description: 5-Substituted uridines, 2-thiouridines and 2-selenouridines represent the most common wobble-positioned bacterial tRNA modifications, with the 5-methylaminomethyl (mnm5 substituent being particularly widespread. Their biological role in the precise recognition of synonymous purine-ending codons is still under investigation. Modified uridines are also known to enhance the stability and base pairing specificity of therapeutic nucleic acids.

title: Unveiling the Future of Neurorehabilitation: Insights from the 18th Congress from the Society for the Study of Neuroprotection and Neuroplasticity (SSNN) in Conjunction with the WFNR-EFNR Central Asia Regional Meeting
creator: Stefana-Andrada Dobran, Alexandra Gherman, Dafin Mureşanu
description: . As this field evolves, traditional approaches intertwine with groundbreaking technological advancements such as virtual reality systems that facilitate immersive therapy or neurostimulation techniques that promote neural plasticity. This convergence of modern and traditional methods creates a new era of comprehensive and highly effective treatment strategies.

title: Correction: Effect of PM2.5 exposure on susceptibility to allergic asthma in elderly rats treated with allergens
creator: Lianlian Zhao, Xiaolin Ding, Li Zhou, Chenchen Song, Taisheng Kang, Yanfeng Xu, Yunpeng Liu, Yunlin Han, Wenjie Zhao, Boxiang Zhang, Dan Xu, Jianguo Guo
description: in the process of preparing the samples, the first and second view of PO group were taken from the same rat. The original Figure 3 and accompanying legend appear below. Effects of PM2.5 exposure on lung injury in elderly rats.

title: Between neurodiversity and therapy: the importance of making conscious and responsible choices in supporting individuals on the autism spectrum
creator: Przemysław Bąbel, Paweł Ostaszewski
description: in the pace and manner of human development, with all its behavioral (including psychological) consequences [1]. Voices advocating for a shift from the previously “medicalized” perspective to accepting the fact that people develop and behave differently are becoming more prominent [2]. This perspective suggests modifying the social conditions in which they function.

title: Mean shift based prototypical network for steel surface anomaly recognition
creator: Canan Tastimur
description: Steel production plays a crucial role in the global economy, and surface defects in hot-rolled steel sheets significantly affect product quality and consumer acceptance. This paper introduces Mean Shift based Prototypical network (MSPro-Net), a novel and effective Prototypical network based on mean drift for classifying surface defects early in the manufacturing process.

title: Hematological biomarkers of troponin, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio serve as effective predictive indicators of high-risk mortality in acute coronary syndrome
creator: Bryan G de Liyis, Angela F Ciaves, Marwa H Intizam, Pierre J Jusuf, I Made J Rina Artha
description: BackgroundAssessing high-risk mortality in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients, encompassing ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI), Non-ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (NSTEMI), and Unstable Angina Pectoris (UAP), is crucial. However, the prognostic significance of hematological parameters in predicting high-risk mortality in ACS patients remains uncertain despite advancements in ACS research.

title: Application of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s Sentinel Routine Querying Tools to the Taiwan Sentinel Data Model-formatted National Health Insurance Research Database
creator: Fang-Ju Lin, Ling-Ya Huang, Chi-Chuan Wang, Sengwee Toh
description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s Sentinel System is a leading distributed data network for drug safety surveillance in the world. The National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) in Taiwan was converted into the Taiwan Sentinel Data Model (TSDM) based on the Sentinel Common Data Model (SCDM) version 6.0.2.

title: Biosynthesized bimetallic nanoparticles containing CeO2 and ZnO exert shape and size dependent anticancer effects
creator: Seyed Mahdi Mousavi, Yaghub Pazhang, Asghar Zamani
description: Bimetallic nanoparticles contain attractive properties because they show simultaneously two metals atom functions. ZnO and CeO2 nanoparticles exhibited biocompatibility and anticancer activity properties. Therefore, we studied the anticancer effect of bimetallic nanoparticles containing ZnO and CeO2 derived from walnut shell powder on colorectal and breast cancer cells.

title: Therapeutic effects of orally administration of viable and inactivated probiotic strains against murine urinary tract infection
creator: Vo Thi Hong Van, Zhen-Shu Liu, Yueh-Jen Hsieh, Wei-Chen Shiu, Bo-Yuan Chen, Yu-We Ku, Po-Wen Chen
description: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are highly prevalent bacterial infections that pose significant health risks. Specific probiotic strains have been recommended for UTI control and management of antibiotic resistance. Otherwise, para-probiotics, defined as inactivated probiotic cells, offer potential advantages by minimizing risks associated with live microorganisms. However, the effectiveness of heat-killed probiotic strains against UTIs remains uncertain.

title: New candidate gene mutations in astrocytoma with seizures
creator: Pongsakorn Choochuen, Natthapon Khongcharoen, Surasak Sangkhathat, Anukoon Kaewborisutsakul, Thara Tunthanathip, Kanitpong Phabphal
description: Seizures are a common presenting symptom in astrocytomas, yet the underlying genomic drivers remain incompletely understood. We performed whole-exome sequencing on tumor tissue from 40 patients with astrocytoma (25 with preoperative seizures, 15 without) to explore somatic mutation profiles associated with seizure occurrence.

title: ASSESSING CATASTROPHIC HEALTHCARE EXPENDITURES IN THE EMERGENCY SURGICAL CARE OF CHILDREN WITH INTUSSUSCEPTION: INSIGHTS FROM A TERTIARY HOSPITAL IN NIGERIA
creator: I Chukwu, S Ekpemo, L Okonkwo, C Uchendu, C Isaac-Chukwu, U Ezomike
description: Background:Emergency and essential surgery should be affordable, accessible, and timely. However, this is not the narrative in our setting as patients present late with complications requiring operative treatment which has an attendant healthcare expenditure often tending towards household income depletion. This study assessed the proportion of patients who incurred catastrophic healthcare expenditures following operative treatment for intussusception in our facility.

title: RESTRICTED DATA MANAGEMENT: THE CURRENT PRACTICE AND THE FUTURE
creator: JOY BOHYUN JANG, AMY M. PIENTA, MARGARET C. LEVENSTEIN, JOE SAUL
description: Many organizations across the world that manage restricted data have adapted the Five Safes framework (safe data, safe projects, safe people, safe setting, safe output) for their management of restricted and confidential data. While the Five Safes have been well integrated throughout the data life cycle, organizations encounter several challenges with regard to safe data management.

title: An update on liver surgery – a new terminology and modern techniques
creator: Verena Tripke, Nils Sommer
description: Liver surgery is the cornerstone of the curative treatment of malignant liver tumors. However, the liver anatomy is very complex, and liver surgery is still associated with relevant morbidity despite many technical advances. The Brisbane nomenclature is used worldwide to classify liver resection. However, this nomenclature has several limitations as multiple terms are used for the same type of resection.

title: Effect of symptom clusters on quality of life in patients with head and neck cancer treated with radiotherapy: a cross-sectional study
creator: Rui Zhao, Tingting Ding, Huili Ma, Yanhui Ma, Ailian He, Jiaxun Kang, Yaosong Zhao
description: Patients with head and neck cancer (HNC) frequently encounter symptom clusters following radiotherapy, which substantially affect their quality of life. This study aims to identify distinct symptom clusters in undergoing radiotherapy HNC patients and examine how self-perceived burden and social support mediate the relationship between symptom clusters and quality of life.

title: INVOLUNTARY CHILDLESSNESS AND ASSISTED CONCEPTION: PERCEPTION AMONGST NURSES AT THE UNIVERSITY COLLEGE HOSPITAL, IBADAN.
creator: OO Saanu, GO Obajimi
description: Introduction:Involuntary childlessness, a pas de deux is perceived as a stigma in many developing countries and often leads to marital disharmony due to the high premium placed on childbearing emanating from deep rooted socio-cultural beliefs. Nurses play a pivotal role in patient management due to their close contact and association with patients and their relatives.

title: Intratesticular copper oxide nanoparticles induce dose-dependent chemical castration in male mice
creator: Amin Rezazadeh, Alireza Najafpour, Ali Soleimanzadeh, Amir Amniattalab
description: Chemical castration represents a non-surgical alternative to achieve male sterility by inducing azoospermia, with growing interest in nanoparticle-based agents owing to their targeted toxicity. This study aimed to determine whether intratesticular administration of copper oxide nanoparticles (CuO NPs) is effective in the chemical castration of male mice, and whether biochemical and histological changes can be assessed.

title: PATHOMORPHOLOGY OF VERRUCAE: A CLINICOPATHOLOGIC STUDY
creator: I Emmanuel, PO Akpa, BV Kwaghe, CN Ibeanu, JB Atiku, IA Othman, NZ Bahaushe, JE Ben, JA Emmanuel, C Amaike, SJ Winnie, T Leslie, TN Fadok
description: Introduction:Verrucae are benign squamous epithelial lesions affecting the skin and mucous membranes, as a result of infection with low-risk Human Papilloma virus, with an estimated 10% of the world's population affected. This work studies the clinicopathology of all histologically diagnosed warts at the Jos University Teaching Hospital between 1st January 2013 and 31st December 2022.

title: THE NATIONAL HEALTH INSURANCE AUTHORITY OF NIGERIA AND IMPLICATIONS FOR UNIVERSAL HEALTH COVERAGE
creator: DA Adewole
description: Background:The National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) of Nigeria was established in the year 2005. The overall objective of the scheme was to enhance access to quality healthcare for all and minimize catastrophic health expenditures. However, since inception, the population coverage has been less than ten percent of the total.

title: Optogenetic stimulation of pyramidal neurons in the rat primary visual cortex modulates ON- and OFF- receptive field areas independently
creator: Jonathan Kozal, Evelina Simkute, Gytis Baranauskas
description: Retinal ganglion cells detect changes in illuminance. An increase and a decrease in illuminance levels induce ON and OFF responses, respectively. This segregation into two major types of visual responses is carried out through the lateral geniculate nucleus (LGN) to the primary visual cortex area V1.

title: Treatment journey of patients with hepatocellular carcinoma using real-world data in British Columbia, Canada
creator: Soo Jin Seung, Hasnain Saherawala, Brandon Zagorski, Carman Tong, Howard Lim, Peter Kim, Vladimir Marquez, Sharlene Gill, David Liu, Janine M Davies
description: Aim:This study examined treatment patterns, survival outcomes and healthcare costs related to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in British Columbia.Methods:The study utilized data from two physician databases (HCC and MOTION) and the provincial British Columbia transplant database.Results:The analysis revealed diverse treatment approaches and identified the varying treatment journeys of patients. Liver transplant and systemic therapies demonstrated improved survival rates.

title: EARLY IMPACTS OF FUEL SUBSIDY REMOVAL ON MENTAL HEALTH STATUS OF PRIMARY HEALTHCARE WORKERS AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS IN NIGERIA: A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY
creator: D Bakare, J Salako, A Sogbesan, A A Bakare
description: Background:The abrupt removal of fuel subsidy in Nigeria led to exponential increase in fuel prices. The resultant economic pressure may have effects on the mental health status of Nigerians. The objective is to understand this impact, we assessed changes in mental health status among primary healthcare workers and community members after fuel subsidy removal.

title: EPHA4 Genetic Variant in a Patient with Epilepsy, Ophthalmological Anomalies, and Neurodevelopmental Delay
creator: M Sleptsova, C Georgiev, S Atemin, P Dimova, D Avdjieva-Tzavella, G Tacheva, I Litvinenko, L Grozdanova, T Todorov, V Mitev, A Todorova
description: We present the findings of a Whole Exome Sequencing in a 2-year-old boy, conceived via In Vitro Fertilization with donor sperm, who suffers from an undiagnosed neurological syndrome. The following heterozygous variant in the EPHA4 gene was identified and classified as likely pathogenic: c.1655_1656, p.(Ser552CysfsTer23).

title: Selected nutritional properties of Ganoderma lucidum and substrate degradation during multi-cycle reuse with hazelnut branch waste
creator: Caglar Akcay
description: In this study, the effects of reusing spent Reishi (Ganoderma lucidum) (Curtis) P. Karst mushroom substrate (SMS) from cultivation—by mixing it with hazelnut branch-based substrate (HB) at different ratios (HB100%, HB75%:SMS25%, HB50%:SMS50%, HB25%:SMS75%, SMS100%)—on the yield, quality, and nutritional composition of mushrooms were investigated. Yield performance, ash contents, and mineral composition of the harvested mushrooms were evaluated.

title: Improving Access to the Transportation Alternatives Program for Rural Communities
creator: Jessica Stroope, Marisa Jones, Brian Nunes, Denise Holston
description: Rural small towns with small main streets and compact downtown development can be ideal locations to create walkable communities. The Centers for Disease Controls and Prevention (CDC)’s High Obesity Program (HOP) funds Cooperative Extension programs to implement strategies to improve food access and support active transportation in high obesity (often rural) counties.

title: Impact of slice thickness on reproducibility of CT radiomic features of lung tumors
creator: Sanat Gupta, Kaushik Nayak, Saikiran Pendem, Tarun Gangil, Mubarak Taiwo Mustapha, Mubarak Taiwo Mustapha, Saikiran Pendem
description: BackgroundRadiomics posits that quantified characteristics from radiographic images reflect underlying pathophysiology. Lung cancer (LC) is one of the prevalent forms of cancer, causing mortality. Slice thickness (ST) of computed tomography (CT) images is a crucial factor influencing the generalizability of radiomic features (RF) in oncology. There is scarcity of research that how ST affects variability of RF in LC.

title: Effect of tele-support on attention levels of emergency medical technicians during simulated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
creator: Vincenz Scharner, Christina Hafner, Philipp Metelka, Lena Reischmann, Josef Michael Lintschinger, Stefan Ulbing, Nikolaus Frimmel, Peter Gröpel, Michael Wagner, Harald Willschke, Alexander Hermann, Martina Hermann
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Telemedicine in the form of a provider-to-provider telemedical application, in which an expert supports the medical team at the patient’s location with medical and non-technical skills is slowly being introduced in preclinical emergency medicine. While the benefit of a tele-team leader could be demonstrated for simulated neonatal resuscitation scenarios, the effect of tele-support for emergency medical technicians (EMTs) on their attention, cognitive load, workload, and performance in case of an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) in adult patients is still unknown.

title: Enhanced amino acid biosynthesis in Phaffia rhodozyma via herbicide-induced selection
creator: Svetlana Raita, Iveta Kuzmika, Taras Mika, Zane Geiba, Kriss Spalvins
description: According to the Food and Agricultural Organisation 2024 statement, developing single-cell protein technology is important to reduce the burden on conventional feed protein production sectors. In this regard, improved commercial strains rich in amino acids, especially Lys and Met, may provide a sustainable alternative source of protein in aquaculture diets.

title: The impact of three amino acids with distinct electrical properties on the synthesis of α-casein by MAC-T cells
creator: Yu Ding, Lewen Xie, Min Yang, Xinyu Zhang, Liang Yang, Wanping Ren, Ruoshan Luo, Yang Yang, Hang Zhang, Wei Shao
description: This study utilized in vitro cultured bovine mammary epithelial cells line(MAC-T cells) to examine how different concentrations of non-polar proline (Pro), polar negatively charged glutamic acid (Glu), and polar uncharged serine (Ser) affect α-casein synthesis. A multi-factor level completely randomized experimental design was adopted.

title: Expression Profiling of ADAMTS (L) Superfamily of Genes in Various Human Eye Tissues
creator: Fatemeh Suri, Abdullah Biginaloo, Mehdi Ghadimi, Hossein Dehghan Banadaki, Seyyed Hassan Paylakhi, Mozhgan Rezaei Kanavi
description: Background:A disintegrin and metalloproteinase with thrombospondin motifs (ADAMTS) is a superfamily of extracellular proteinases found in both mammals and invertebrates. Although there is some evidence about the role of ADAMTSs in ocular diseases such as glaucoma and ectopia lentis, but there is little information about the expression patterns of ADAMTS-1–20 and ADAMTS-like (ADAMTSL-1–6 and PAPLN) genes in human ocular tissues.

title: Exploring the Physical and Mental Health Challenges of Teenage Pregnancy: A Qualitative Study in the Tamale Metropolis, Ghana
creator: Rafatu Tahiru, Comfort Kona, Abiba Nyari, Tawfik Mohammed, Dorothy Anukem Pawmang
description: Objective:Teenage pregnancy poses significant public health challenges globally, particularly affecting the physical and mental well-being of adolescent girls. Despite a global decline in teenage birth rates, regions like sub-Saharan Africa continue to experience high prevalence. In Ghana’s Tamale metropolis, teenage pregnancy rates have shown a concerning rise, underscoring the need for an in-depth exploration of its multifaceted impacts.

title: Near-infrared photobiomodulation stimulates viability and cartilage matrix synthesis in human chondrocytes
creator: Sofia Oliveira, Débora Ferreira, Jorge Padrão, Susana O Catarino, Francisca Monteiro, Andrea Zille, Ligia R Rodrigues, Filipe S Silva, Betina B Hinckel, Óscar Carvalho, Ana Leal
description: Photobiomodulation (PBM) within red to near-infrared spectrum has been proposed as a method to restore articular cartilage injuries, due to its ability to modulate effectively chondrocyte activity, namely viability, proliferation and extracellular matrix synthesis. This in vitro study aimed to determine the most appropriate PBM dosage on human chondrocytes.

title: Small GTPase Rac promotes hyphal formation and microconidiogenesis in Trichophyton rubrum
creator: Masaki Ishii, Shinya Ohata
description: Morphogenesis plays a pivotal role in the infection process of Trichophyton rubrum, a primary aetiological agent of dermatophytosis that inhabits superficial human tissues. T. rubrum proliferates by extending filamentous structures, or hyphae, which are composed of highly polarized cells. In response to environmental stimuli, T. rubrum also produces asexual spores called microconidia, consisting of individual cells.

title: Smoking Cessation Success and Affecting Factors in Geriatric Patients
creator: Pelin Duru Çetinkaya, Ayşe Turan, Pelin Pinar Deniz, Ferhat Çetinkaya, Seren Arpaz, Atilla Uysal, Seyhan Dülger, Banu Salepçi, Oğuz Kilinç, Aslı Görek Dilektaşlı
description: Background:There are difficulties in the treatment of smoking cessation in elderly patients. However, elderly smokers who gave up smoking had lower rates of death from heart attack, stroke, and cancer, as well as improved cognitive function. This study aimed to investigate the affecting factors and the success of smoking cessation rate in patients aged 60 and over in Turkey.

title: Kinesin genes KIF4A, KIF20A and KIF11 as prognostic biomarkers in lung adenocarcinoma by integrative bioinformatic analysis and experimental validation
creator: Huanqin Wang, Lu Zhou, Fengxiang Huang
description: lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) causes a large number of deaths worldwide each year. The pivotal involvement of Kinesin superfamily proteins (KIFs) plays a critical role in the progression of LUAD. This study primarily investigates the biological functionalities associated with specific genes within the KIF family while concurrently developing prognostic signatures of LUAD.

title: SENSING SPOUSAL CARE DYADS’ ACTIVITY PATTERNS: TWO NOVEL DYADIC METRICS FOR CAPTURING TIME USE
creator: Lyndsey Miller, Wan-Tai Au-Yeung, Karen Lyons, Joel Steele, Jeffrey Kaye
description: Spousal care dyads’ in-home activity and routines are typically captured through self-report. Remote passive sensing offers a sensitive, continuous, and ecologically-valid method of assessment that increases the ability to detect patterns of daily activities and function; however, there are challenges of deploying these technologies among dyads in the community setting and in the context of dementia.

title: Dietary Patterns and Cardiovascular Risk: Are the Mediterranean Diet, the Heart-Healthy Diet, and Phytochemicals Associated with Lower Cardiovascular Risks?
creator: Hande Bakırhan, Serap İncedal Irgat
description: Background:Dietary pattern may be one of the determinants of cardiovascular health. This study aimed to examine the relationship between a heart-healthy diet, the phytochemical content of a diet, and Mediterranean diet and cardiovascular disease (CVD) risks.Methods:This study was conducted with healthy volunteers (n=1446) from Turkey between August 2022 and September 2022.

title: Morphophysiological and antioxidant enzymatic mechanisms of seven Axonopus compressus variants grown under water stress conditions
creator: Ting Zeng, Abdul Shukor Juraimi, Nazatul Shima Naharudin, Mahmudul Hasan, Muhammad Saiful Ahmad-Hamdani
description: This study evaluated the morphological and physiological responses of a turfgrass species, namely the common Axonopus compressus and its six new variants to three soil water conditions, aiming to understand the performance and resilience of this turfgrass under climate-driven drought pressures.

title: Bibliometric Analysis of Published Original Research Articles on Leisure Constraints between 1991 and 2019
creator: Elif Köse, Tennur Yerlisu-Lapa, Hüseyin Gökçe, Kostas Alexandris, Ali Serdar Yücel
description: Background:The decrease in the frequency and duration of participation in leisure activities has negative effects on the physical, cognitive and psychological health of individuals. In this context, identifying the obstacles, which prevent individuals from participating in leisure activities, may offer important clues to institutions and organizations in taking measures to increase participation.Methods:The bibliometric analysis method was used in this study.

title: Air pollution abatement from Green-Blue-Grey infrastructure
creator: Prashant Kumar, Karina Corada, Sisay E. Debele, Ana Paula Mendes Emygdio, KV Abhijith, Hala Hassan, Parya Broomandi, Richard Baldauf, Nerea Calvillo, Shi-Jie Cao, Sylvane Desrivières, Zhuangbo Feng, John Gallagher, Thomas Rodding Kjeldsen, Anwar Ali Khan, Mukesh Khare, Sri Harsha Kota, Baizhan Li, S
description: Green-blue-grey infrastructure (GBGI) offers environmental benefits in urban areas, yet its impact on air pollution is under-researched, and the literature fragmented. This review evaluates quantitative studies on GBGI’s capability to mitigate air pollution, compares their specific pollutant removal processes, and identifies areas for further investigation. Of the 51 GBGI types reviewed, only 22 provided quantitative pollution reduction data.

title: Improved reannotations of Aegilops umbellulata (PI 554389) genome and transcriptomics data provide candidates for leaf rust resistance for wheat improvement
creator: Jatinder Singh, Santosh Gudi, Peter J Maughan, Rajeev Gupta, Upinder Gill
description: Leaf rust caused by Puccinia triticina is a yield limiting disease of cultivated wheat throughout the world. Ae. umbellulata is a diploid species of wheat wild relatives containing high genetic diversity for resistance to multiple races of leaf rust. Here, we used short-read data along with long-read transcript data to reannotate (version 2) the Ae. umbellulata acc.

title: 牙周辅助加速成骨正畸治疗的研究进展
creator: 奕宸 熊, 珺 陈, 文杰 李
description: 牙周辅助加速成骨正畸治疗(periodontally accelerated osteogenic orthodontics，PAOO)是正畸治疗的辅助手段，其基础原理为“局部加速现象”，即通过促进破骨细胞的活动达到加速正畸治疗的目的。在临床应用上，其手术方法近年来逐步优化，包括压电骨皮质切开术、牙槽骨微穿孔术等新术式的应用。所使用的材料也逐渐改良，包括生物活性玻璃等新型移植材料和富血小板纤维蛋白膜等新型屏障膜。正是由于这些临床创新的涌现，PAOO正朝着低痛苦、低损伤、高疗效的方向发展。但是，目前关于PAOO的临床研究尚少，未来仍需大样本、多中心的随机对照试验来评价不同术式、不同植骨材料等对PAOO临床疗效的影响。 牙周辅助加速成骨正畸治疗(periodontally accelerated osteogenic orthodontics，PAOO)是在传统的正畸治疗中，加入了切开牙槽骨骨皮质的措施，从而达到加速正畸牙移动的目的[1]。PAOO在最初被提出时，是一种仅包含翻瓣手术后骨皮质切开操作的正畸加速手术。然而，鉴于其会对患者的牙槽骨造成较大损伤，且会引起诸多不良反应，此手术方法未能得以推广。随着其在临床应用中被不断改良，以Wilcko团队[2]将植骨引入该手术为标志，当下广义的PAOO还包括了植骨、放膜等一系列步骤，兼具改善牙周状况、重塑牙槽骨的功能，较大程度减小了手术的风险。因此，如今广义的PAOO不仅可以加速正畸牙移动，也可以实现牙槽骨与牙龈软组织增厚，减少正畸并发症，扩大正畸治疗适应范围。在中国预期接受正畸治疗与已经接受治疗的患者中，因人种的原因有较大比例患者存在骨开窗、骨开裂等骨缺损情况[3]。因此，PAOO在中国具有较大的临床应用前景。 本文旨在系统综述PAOO的临床及基础研究进展，以期深入探讨该技术的作用机制、临床应用及未来发展方向，提高临床医师、研究人员对其的认知水平，促进其在临床实践和科研探索中的应用与发展。 PAOO技术基础原理概述 PAOO及其衍生改良后的手术方式的基础原理皆源自Frost[4]于1983年提出的“局部加速现象”(regional acceleratory phenomenon，RAP)理论。该技术借助骨皮质切开这一手术方式，破坏牙槽骨骨质，刺激牙周组织内产生炎症反应，成骨细胞核因子κB配体受体(receptor activator for nuclear factor-κB ligand，RANKL)表达升高，其与破骨前体细胞表面的RANK结合，诱导术区破骨前体细胞成熟[5]，并且使成骨细胞相关因子表达增加，如骨钙蛋白、骨钙素、载脂蛋白A-I(apolipoprotein A-I，APOA-I)等[6-7]，进而降低术区骨密度，一定程度上减少了正畸牙移动的阻力，实现加速正畸牙移动。 PAOO后的生理学机制是该领域的研究热点，目前提出了PAOO的多种机制。Zhang等[8]提出，在PAOO后，由于miRNA-21表达水平升高，程序性细胞死亡因子4(programmed cell death 4，PDCD4)基因表达降低，导致c-Fos蛋白水平升高，RANKL介导的破骨细胞生成增强，牙槽骨重塑，牙槽骨骨质暂时性减少，正畸牙移动加快。Wang等[9]的研究表明，miRNA-21通过抑制磷酸酯酶与张力蛋白同源物(phosphatase and tensin homolog，PTEN)对磷脂酰肌醇3激酶/蛋白激酶B(phosphatidylinositol 3 kinase/protein kinase B，PI3K/Akt)信号转导通路的抑制作用，从而加快破骨细胞生成，促进在PAOO后正畸牙的加速移动。Kinjo等[10]对于牙槽骨微穿孔术(micro-osteoperforations，MOPs)的研究表明：在骨皮质受到刺激后，牙周韧带细胞会产生大量炎症因子，如肿瘤坏死因子-α(tumor necrosis factor-α，TNF-α)等，这些炎症因子可刺激基质细胞提高RANKL的生成量，从而诱导破骨细胞的生成，加速正畸牙移动(图1)。以上研究大致勾勒出了PAOO后的牙周物质变化以及部分物质对于加速正畸治疗的生物学作用，然而还需要进一步探究术后牙周组织变化情况以完全阐明PAOO的完整生物学机制。 PAOO效果通路示意图 Figure 1 Illustration of the PAOO effect pathway APOA1: Apolipoprotein A1;
