description: A cross-sectional descriptive study was carried out on a study population of 81 goat herds to investigate the prevalence and frequency of two single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs; E198A and F200Y) associated with resistance to benzimidazoles (BZ) in Haemonchus contortus populations of goats in Poland.

title: Description and biomechanical evaluation of the modified laparoscopic-assisted percutaneous gastropexy technique in dogs
creator: Dong Woo Kim, Ho Hyun Kwak, Junhyung Kim, Heung Myong Woo
description: BackgroundTotal laparoscopic gastropexy (TLG) has become increasingly popular due to its minimally invasive nature, requiring only three ports and no additional skin incisions aside from those for port placement. However, a notable limitation of TLG is the difficulty and time required for intracorporeal suturing. To address this challenge, we investigated a new technique—modified laparoscopic-assisted percutaneous gastropexy (mLAPG)—in canine cadavers.

title: Formation of hydroxyapatite on tooth surfaces by calcium hypophosphite in saliva
creator: Pascal Fandrich, Erik Schulze zur Wiesche, Bennett Tochukwu Amaechi, Joachim Enax
description: AimThis in vitro study aimed to investigate whether calcium hypophosphite (CaP) mediates hydroxyapatite (HAP) formation in artificial and human saliva and, in a proof-of-principle toothbrushing model, promotes mineral deposition and occlusion of dentinal tubules.MethodsA CaP solution was added to artificial saliva and human saliva, respectively. The resulting precipitate was analyzed using X-ray powder diffraction (XRD).

title: Delayed diagnosis leading to severe complications in primary hyperparathyroidism caused by atypical parathyroid tumor
creator: Francesca Lacchè, Alessandro Ciarloni, Monia Bordoni, Gianmaria Salvio, Giancarlo Balercia, Gilberta Giacchetti
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Severe skeletal complications at the onset of primary hyperparathyroidism are uncommon in contemporary Western clinical practice because routine serum calcium measurement usually allows early diagnosis. We describe a case of primary hyperparathyroidism in which delayed diagnosis, despite suggestive symptoms, led to an extremely severe presentation characterized by multiple fractures, osteolytic lesions, and prolonged postsurgical hungry bone syndrome requiring several months of intensive treatments and hospitalization. During hospitalization, the patient developed potentially life-threatening infectious and thrombotic complications.

title: Impact of Preoperative Chronic Opioid Use on Postoperative Outcomes Following Lumbar Fusion: A Nationwide Analysis
creator: Atef F Hulliel, Dana Saleh, Ahmad Zayd Alkadri, David J Boughanem, Rafal Chociej, Freddie Rodriguez Beato, Srujan Kopparapu, Patrick Kim, Mohsen Rostami, Puya Alikhani
description: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectivesChronic opioid use is common among patients undergoing lumbar fusion, and preoperative use has been linked to worse postoperative outcomes. However, much of this evidence derives from administrative datasets with limited ability to adjust for mental health.

title: A curved-beam piezoelectric MEMS resonator featuring multiple temperature plateaus with enhanced stability
creator: Yancheng Lian, Yueyang Li, Fangzhou Chen, Zhuoyue Zheng, Jinuo Zhou, Junchen Liu, Fengzhe Xu, Jinbo Yang, Jianlin Chen, Chen Wang, Michael Kraft, Ka-Meng Lei, R P Martins, Pui-In Mak, Yuan Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Silicon-based Micro-electromechanical Systems (MEMS) resonators face stability challenges due to their temperature susceptibility, which impedes the advancement towards high-precision applications. This work reports a multi-modal curved-beam piezoelectric resonator that enhances frequency stability through engineered irregular geometry and mechanical nonlinearity. Utilizing a standard Silicon-On-Insulator (SOI) - Aluminum Nitride (AlN) process, the proposed device engenders 17 vibration modes within 5 MHz, addressing the detection constraints and information extraction of non-inplane modes for capacitive counterparts and circumventing the needs of vacuum encapsulation.

title: Competency-based training in anaesthesiology: train the trainers first. A descriptive cross-sectional survey by the committee of the European Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care (ESAIC) Teach the Teachers Masterclass
creator: Vojislava Neskovic, Carmen Oliveira, Aeyal Raz, Lesley Bromley, Gordana Jovanovic
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionThe level of competence in teaching among trainers expected to deliver training according to the European Training Requirement in anaesthesiology is unknown. The aim of this descriptive cross-sectional survey, performed from 1 September 2021 until 31 October 2021, and promoted by the European Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care (ESAIC) was to establish the current level of knowledge and faculty development among European countries regarding competency-based education and training (CBMET) in anesthesia and intensive care.ResultsA total of 711 responses of anaesthesiologists working

title: Mechanical ventilation–associated AKI: toward a multimodal and kidney-protective ventilatory framework
creator: Ying Gao, Yipeng Fang, Silvia De Rosa, Michele Salvagno, Lina Zhao, Keliang Xie, Fabio Silvio Taccone
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Mechanical ventilation–associated acute kidney injury (AKI) represents a complex manifestation of lung–kidney cross-talk driven by hemodynamic alterations, neurohumoral activation, systemic inflammation and disturbances in gas exchange and acid–base homeostasis. Beyond static ventilatory settings, increasing evidence suggests that dynamic fluctuations in airway and perfusion parameters, including static driving pressure (ΔP), positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), mean airway pressure (Pmean), and effective renal perfusion pressure (eRPP) may substantially influence renal vulnerability during mechanical ventilation.

title: Evaluation of host-immune biomarker signatures as multiplex qPCR diagnostic assays: a pilot study toward meeting WHO target product profiles for TB diagnosis in India
creator: Harriet N. Garlant, Kalaiarasan Ellappan, Noyal Mariya Joseph, Carrie Turner, Vishnukanth Govindaraj, Saka Vinod Kumar, Sanjeev Kumar, Seshadri Vasan, Karen E. Kempsell
description: BackgroundTuberculosis (TB) remains the leading cause of death from a single infectious agent. Current diagnostic tools are limited, especially in low-resource settings. The World Health Organization's (WHO) Target Product Profiles (TPPs) call for rapid, non-sputum-based diagnostics with high sensitivity and specificity.

title: Parental involvement, self-efficacy, and learning motivation of hearing-impaired students: insights from Savelugu, Ghana
creator: Isaac Nyame, Mary Nyeyem Issah, Sampson Mante, Christiana Nyarko Adjei, Diana Baapeng
description: The educational development of learners with Hearing Impairment (HI) remains a significant concern within inclusive education systems, especially in low-resource countries. The influence of parental involvement and academic self-efficacy on motivation to learn is considered important, but their relationship has not been thoroughly examined in Sub-Saharan Africa.

title: Persistent Hypoxia After Tricuspid Valve Replacement
creator: John Nguyen, Thomas Merino, Vijay Kandula, Leticia Castillo Kontak, Raul Mercado Garcia, Angel Caldera, Aditi Shankar, Rafael Gonzalez, Soumya Neravetla, Jose F Condado
description: BackgroundTranscatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) is a novel therapy for symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation in high-risk surgical patients. Platypnea-orthopnea syndrome has not previously been described as a complication of TTVR.Case SummaryA 76-year-old woman with symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation underwent successful TTVR but developed persistent hypoxia despite negative pulmonary work-up. Her hypoxia followed a platypnea-orthodeoxia pattern.

title: Risk factors for multiple bronchoalveolar lavage procedures in children with severe or refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia
creator: Chaolei Yang, Guitao Li, Ying Zhu, Yong Wang, Lei Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo identify factors influencing how often bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) is performed in children with severe or refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP) and provide evidence to guide early intervention.MethodsClinical data for 271 children with severe or refractory MPP who underwent BAL at the studied institution between May 1, 2023, and April 30, 2024, were retrospectively divided according to the number of BAL procedures into a single-treatment group (STG, n = 219) and a multiple-treatment group (≥ 2 times; MTG, n = 52).

title: Depression and anxiety symptoms among women in post-conflict Somalia: a cross-sectional study in maternal and child health centres
creator: Gallad D. Hassan, Juweria N. L. Abshir, Fatumo Osman
description: ObjectiveMental health issues can be regarded as a severe public health problem that affects low-, middle-, and high-income countries worldwide. However, certain populations in post-conflict countries may have particularly vulnerable mental health, such as women of childbearing age in Somalia.

title: Pediatric oncology drug development and dosage optimization
creator: S. Y. Amy Cheung, Justin L. Hay, Yu-Wei Lin, Rik de Greef, Julie Bullock
description: Oncology drug discovery and development has always been an area facing many challenges. Phase 1 oncology studies are typically small, open-label, sequential studies enrolling a small sample of adult patients (i.e., 3-6 patients/cohort) in dose escalation. Pediatric evaluations typically lag behind the adult development program.

title: Cancer Treatment During Pregnancy and Maternal and Infant Outcomes: A Descriptive Cohort Study Using a Japanese Claims Database
creator: Masami Tsuchiya, Tomofumi Ishikawa, Takamasa Sakai, Satoko Hori, Taku Obara
description: PurposeTo characterize cancer treatment during pregnancy and maternal and infant outcomes among women with cancer identified during pregnancy in Japan.MethodsIn this descriptive cohort study, we used mother‐infant linkage data from the JMDC claims database from 2005 to 2024. Live‐birth pregnancies were considered eligible when a malignant neoplasm (ICD‐10 C00–C97) was recorded between the estimated pregnancy onset and delivery.

title: Impact of Incidental Durotomy on Health Care Resource Utilization Following Posterior Cervical Decompression and Fusion
creator: Mitchell K Ng, Leonidas E Mastrokostas, Paul G Mastrokostas, Eli Berglas, Matthew W Xie, Masataka Mizuno, Imran Kyeso, Avi Gupta, Jesse M Galina, Arie Monas, Jorden Xavier, Sarah Brauer, Pemla Jagtiani, Jad Bou Monsef, Afshin E Razi, Daniel R Fassett, Andrew P Alvarez, Nicholas U Ahn, Mark F Kurd, I
description: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectivesTo evaluate the national incidence and hospitalization impact of incidental durotomy following elective posterior cervical decompression and fusion (PCDF), with respect to complications, length of stay (LOS), costs, and discharge disposition.MethodsAdults undergoing elective PCDF were identified in the 2016–2022 National Inpatient Sample.

title: Maize STEM BENDING1 controls plant architecture through cell wall and auxin pathways
creator: Shiya Zhao, Babar Farid, Xintong Liu, Liang Dong, Fang Yang
description: Crop yield is largely determined by plant architecture. Identifying the key genes responsible for maize architecture can help optimize plant architecture for high-density planting. Here, we characterized a dominant stem bending mutant (Stb1) in maize, which exhibited bent stems and curved leaves leading to a slanted architecture. Genetic mapping delimited Stb1 to a 3.7 Mb interval on chromosome 1.

title: Fully automated diaphragm segmentation on routine 2D-cine and 3D thoracic MRI: multireader validation
creator: Samia Boussouar, Alexiane Pasquier, Damien Vaurs, Arthur Dilane Douho Kamta, Anna Reitmann, Nicoletta Pasi, Victoria Donciu, Sara Benchara, Tatiana Wong, Myriam Belghiti, Ithar Gharmaoui, Rose-Marie Dubuisson, Angéline Nemeth, Vincent Lebon, Claire Pellot-Barakat, Marie Poirier-Quinot, Xavier Maître
description: ObjectiveThe diaphragm is central to respiratory mechanics and may be impaired in various diseases. Parametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) assessment is limited by time-consuming manual segmentation. We developed and validated fully automated diaphragm segmentation on two-dimensional (2D)-cine and three-dimensional (3D) thoracic MRI.Materials and methodsIn this single-center study, eligible adults without known diaphragmatic disorders underwent 2D-cine MRI, 3D MRI, or both.

title: Relevance theory and the social realities of communication
creator: Marilynn Johnson
description: A central tenet of theories of meaning in the Gricean tradition—such as Relevance Theory—is that others will come to believe certain things simply by recognizing our intentions to communicate. In this article I demonstrate that this is not equally the case for all interlocutors; some bear additional burdens. In particular, I argue that this can happen in two ways.

title: Expanded characterization of the valproic acid zebrafish larval model of autism spectrum disorder: Insights into dysregulation in the gut
creator: Lesha Pretorius, Johanna Adriana Coetzee, Alexio Pedro dos Santos, Carine Smith
description: BackgroundRelative lack of data on mechanisms underpinning poor gastrointestinal (GI) health in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) limits patient management strategies. Although the valproic acid (VPA) model of ASD is widely used, a comprehensive profile of the model in zebrafish is still lacking, and almost no data are available on ASD‐like GI symptomology or underlying mechanisms.

title: Neurodiversity: post-cognitivist foundations of the 3E approach for educational inclusion of autistic students with technology
creator: Ronnie Videla, May Britt Aros, Francisco Parada, Leonie Kausel, Eduardo Sandoval-Obando, Daniela Jorquera, David Ibacache, Sebastián Maluenda, Pablo Rodríguez-Herrero, Carola Cerpa, María Jesús González, Marcelo Chávez, Paola Ramírez
description: The concept of neurodiversity has gained strength in the last years to highlight the value of individual differences based on relevant variations in brain functioning. Inclusive education has embraced neurodiversity to promote a culture centered on valuing diversity, in response to clinical models based on deficits or disorders.

title: A Comprehensive Self-Medication Management System to Reduce Medication Errors Among People Living With Dementia: Mixed Methods Feasibility and Usability Study
creator: Santosh Basapur, Charles Gellman, Jamie B Plenge, Amelia Troutman, Erin Yurko, Brandon Woolsey, Justin McClendon, Lisa Marceau, Neelum T Aggarwal
description: BackgroundMedication adherence is a critical challenge for people living with dementia and their caregivers. Standard care relies on appropriate medication management, yet there are few effective options beyond manual pill-counting and caregiver-administered dosing. These methods are prone to errors and impose a significant burden.

title: Pathways to the development of purpose in life among ethnic minority adolescents
creator: Rosa Kim, Meeyoung O Min, Sarah L Canham, Morgan Williams
description: Purpose in life has been defined as a sense of meaning, direction, and commitment to valued long‐term goals. Developing a sense of purpose in life is an important task during adolescence and considered an essential developmental asset. However, current understandings of how adolescents, particularly those with an ethnic minority background, develop their life purpose remain limited.

title: Application of next-generation sequencing to identify different pathogens
creator: Aljuboori M. Nafea, Yuer Wang, Duanyang Wang, Ahmed M. Salama, Manal A. Aziz, Shan Xu, Yigang Tong
description: Early and precise detection and identification of various pathogens are essential for epidemiological monitoring, disease management, and reducing the prevalence of clinical infectious diseases. Traditional pathogen detection techniques, which include mass spectrometry, biochemical tests, molecular testing, and culture-based methods, are limited in application and are time-consuming. Next generation sequencing (NGS) has emerged as an essential technology for identifying pathogens.

title: Design of an implementation research study for a digital omnichannel community engagement and risk communication intervention for the prevention and control of vector-borne diseases in India: the OMNIVEC-India study protocol
creator: Rashmi Rodrigues, Amey Dhatrak, Madhusmita Bal, Melari Shisha Nongrum, Neeraj Kumar, Rajiv Sarkar, Twinkle Agrawal, Anuj Mundra, Ira Praharaj, Jyoti Singh, Mrunali Zode, Sudipto Roy, Vani Kandpal, Tanica Lyngdoh, Omnivec Study Team
description: IntroductionVector-borne diseases (VBDs), such as malaria, dengue, and lymphatic filariasis, pose significant public health challenges in India, contributing significantly to the nation’s morbidity and mortality. In this scenario, digital technology promises scalable, contextual, and user-centric interventions for behavior change. However, systematic and comprehensive community-based digital approaches for VBD prevention in India are limited.

title: Clinical, social, molecular, and genetic predictors of cognitive resilience in long-living adults without dementia
creator: Ekaterina Spektor, Aleksandra Mamchur, Mariia Bruttan, Liliya Artemieva, Antonina Rumyantseva, Lorena Matkava, Mikhail Ivanov, Veronika Daniel, Sergey Igorevich Mitrofanov, Irina Strazhesko, Vladimir Yudin, Valentin Makarov, Anton Keskinov, Olga Tkacheva, Daria Kashtanova, Sergey Yudin, Veronika Skv
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundLong-living adults often maintain cognitive function despite neuropathological changes, which is often attributed to cognitive resilience (CR)—a combined effect of cognitive and cerebral reserves. CR is influenced by genetic, clinical, sociodemographic, and environmental factors.Materials and methodsWe investigated genetic, clinical, and environmental predictors of CR in 198 dementia-free long-living adults via two neuropsychological examinations over a 2-year period, a geriatric assessment, and a genome-wide association study (GWAS).ResultsLimited mobility, reduced walking, hearing impairment, depression, anemia, lower quality of life, and decreased BMI were key

title: Factors affecting equitable access and uptake of COVID-19 vaccines in Ghana: a scoping review
creator: James Akazili, Dominic Anaseba, Samuel Chatio, Michel Adurayi Amenah, Daniel Malik Achala, Senait Aleamyehu Beshah, Chijioke O. Nwosu, Nyasha Masuka, John Thato Tlhakanelo, Ifeanyi Chikezie, Elizabeth Naa Adukwei Adote, Grace Njeri Muriithi, John Ele-Ojo Ataguba
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe coronavirus disease (COVID-19) emerged as one of the most serious pandemics that impacted health systems and world economies. Vaccination against the pandemic was considered as an effective tool for the prevention and containment of the virus. Following the outbreak of the Coronavirus pandemic, efforts were made to enhance procurement and distribution of vaccines across countries with the view to containing the pandemic. However, evidence suggested that several factors hindered access, acceptance and use of the COVID-19 vaccines across the globe.

title: Large language model assistance for report-based carotid plaque AHA classification: a multi-reader study
creator: Mengfei Wang, Yixiao Tang, Yulu Yang, Yifan Tu, Zhongzheng Cao, Runjianya Ling, Kaiyue Sun, Jian Ma, Zhicheng Zhang, Ruipeng Zhang, Xiaoer Wei, Dan Wang, Yuehua Li
description: ObjectivesTo evaluate whether large language model assistance improves radiologists’ agreement with a text-based reference standard in inferring the modified American Heart Association carotid plaque classification from free-text MRI reports, and whether a lightweight model can perform well under criteria-guided prompting.Materials and methodsThis retrospective study included 433 patients from three institutions.

title: Deep learning and explainable AI for classification of potato leaf diseases
creator: Sarah M. Alhammad, Doaa Sami Khafaga, Walaa M. El-hady, Farid M. Samy, Khalid M. Hosny
description: The accurate classification of potato leaf diseases plays a pivotal role in ensuring the health and productivity of crops. This study presents a unified approach for addressing this challenge by leveraging the power of Explainable AI (XAI) and transfer learning within a deep Learning framework.

title: Comparative efficacy of trastuzumab deruxtecan versus guideline-recommended treatments for 2L+ unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-mutant non-small cell lung cancer: a systematic review and indirect treatment comparison
creator: Federico Cappuzzo, Lirong Zhang, Kyle Dunton, Natalie Dennis, Pauline Le Nouveau, Agathe Nevière, Aline Gauthier
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionThe clinical benefit of trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd 5.4mg/kg), the first approved HER2-directed therapy for patients with previously treated HER2-mutant (HER2m) non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), was demonstrated in the phase II DESTINY-Lung02 trial.

title: Quantifying the spatial patterns of retinal ganglion cell loss and progression in optic neuropathy by applying a deep learning variational autoencoder approach to optical coherence tomography
creator: Jui-Kai Wang, Brett A. Johnson, Zhi Chen, Honghai Zhang, David Szanto, Brian Woods, Michael Wall, Young H. Kwon, Edward F. Linton, Andrew Pouw, Mark J. Kupersmith, Mona K. Garvin, Randy H. Kardon
description: IntroductionGlaucoma, optic neuritis (ON), and non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) produce distinct patterns of retinal ganglion cell (RGC) damage. We propose a booster Variational Autoencoder (bVAE) to capture spatial variations in RGC loss and generate latent space (LS) montage maps that visualize different degrees and spatial patterns of optic nerve bundle injury.

title: Water and nitrogen regulation strategy for wolfberry farmland based on nitrogen balance in the Yellow River irrigation districts of Gansu Province, China
creator: Minhua Yin, Rongrong Tian, Yi Ling, Yuqing Yang, Yanlin Ma, Yanxia Kang, Guangping Qi, Jinghai Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Agricultural production frequently encounters challenges, including soil nitrogen pollution and imbalances resulting from improper irrigation and fertilization practices. This study focuses on wolfberry farmland, analyzing the effects of four irrigation levels [full irrigation (W0, 75%−85% θf), mild water deficit (W1, 65%−75% θf), moderate water deficit (W2, 55%−65% θf), and severe water deficit (W3, 45%−55% θf)] and four nitrogen application levels [no nitrogen application (N0, 0 kg·ha−1), low nitrogen application (N1, 150 kg·ha−1), medium nitrogen application (N2, 300 kg·ha−1), and high nitrogen application

title: Leveraging AI to automate detection and quantification of extrachromosomal DNA to decode drug responses
creator: Kohen Goble, Aarav Mehta, Damien Guilbaud, Jacob Fessler, Jingting Chen, William Nenad, Christina G. Ford, Oliver Cope, Darby Cheng, William Dennis, Nithya Gurumurthy, Yue Wang, Kriti Shukla, Elizabeth Brunk
description: IntroductionTraditional drug discovery efforts primarily target rapid, reversible protein-mediated adaptations to counteract cancer cell resistance. However, cancer cells also utilize DNA-based strategies, often perceived as slow, irreversible changes like point mutations or drug-resistant clone selection. Extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA), in contrast, represents a rapid, reversible, and predictable DNA alteration critical for cancer’s adaptive response.

title: Metabolic Changes During a Calorie‐Restricted, Fish‐Rich Ketogenic Diet Associated With Increased Circulating TMAO in Healthy Adults
creator: Katarzyna Siedzik, Kamil Góral, Damian Flis, Maciej Jaguszewski, Robert A Olek, Wiesław Ziółkowski
description: BackgroundA ketogenic diet (KD) is increasingly investigated as a nutritional approach for improving glycemic control and metabolic health. However, relatively few studies have examined fish‐rich ketogenic interventions. Fish consumption may substantially increase circulating trimethylamine N‐oxide (TMAO), while habitual fish intake is generally associated with favourable cardiometabolic outcomes. The metabolic significance of a short‐term diet‐induced increase in TMAO therefore remains unclear.

title: The first rodent behavioral study (1822) and the diffusion of human-bred albino rats and mice in the 19th century
creator: Raffaele d’Isa
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Rodents, in particular rats and mice, are currently the most widely employed animal models in psychology and behavioral neuroscience. Nevertheless, an interesting historical question is: when was the first rodent behavioral study performed and by whom?

title: Prehabilitation during neoadjuvant therapy in patients with cancer of the upper gastrointestinal tract and rectum—the study protocol
creator: Irina Chmelova, Dalibor Pastucha, Tomas Hudecek, Zdenek Guran, Sona Ciecotkova, Lubomír Martínek, Jana Zubikova, Alena Matlova, Jakub Dolezel, Dana Salounova, Jakub Chmelo
description: AimsThe concept of prehabilitation, defined as interventions aimed at enhancing a patient's functional capacity prior to an impending physiological stressor, may contribute to reduced postoperative morbidity and mortality. The study's goal is to verify or refute the feasibility of a prehabilitation programme for two diagnostic patient groups during neoadjuvant chemo(radio)therapy, which is prescribed before the scheduled surgical procedure.

title: Cerebral microvascular density, blood-brain barrier permeability, and support for neuroinflammation indicate early aging in a Marfan syndrome mouse model
creator: Tala Curry-Koski, Liam P. Curtin, Mitra Esfandiarei, Theresa Currier Thomas
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionMarfan Syndrome (MFS) is a connective tissue disorder due to mutations in fibrillin-1 (Fbn1), where a Fbn1 missense mutation (Fbn1 C1039G/+ ) can result in systemic increases in the bioavailability and signaling of transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β). In a well-established mouse model of MFS (Fbn1 C1041G/+ ), pre-mature aging of the aortic wall and the progression of aortic root aneurysm are observed by 6-month-of-age. TGF-β signaling has been implicated in cerebrovascular dysfunction, loss of blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, and age-related neuroinflammation.

title: Case report: JAK inhibitor treatment of immune dysregulation symptoms in a patient with PTPN2 deficiency
creator: Anna Roppelt, Ulyana Markina, Irina Beloglazova, Vasily Parshin, Dmitry Kanner, Dmitry Pershin, Mariia Fadeeva, Elena Raykina, Maxim Aleksenko, Alexander Karaulov, Mariana Lysenko, Daria Fomina
description: A heterozygous mutation in the PTPN2 gene has recently been described in several patients exhibiting symptoms of immune dysregulation. The gene encodes a ubiquitous non-receptor T-cell protein tyrosine phosphatase that exerts a negative feedback on the JAK–STAT pathway. Limited clinical data are available advocating the use of JAK inhibitors as an effective treatment for autoimmune complications of PTPN2 deficiency.

title: Mechanism of mTOR/RILP-regulated autophagic flux in increased susceptibility to myocardial ischemia-reperfusion in diabetic mice
creator: Jiyao Zhao, Wei Shi, Yan Zheng, Junjie Wang, Muzhao Yuan, Yultuz Anwar, Yuxuan He, Haiping Ma, Jianjiang Wu
description: BackgroundThe increased myocardial vulnerability that occurs in diabetic patients following an ischemia-reperfusion injury (I/RI) represents a significant perioperative safety risk. A comprehensive understanding of the intrinsic mechanisms underlying this phenomenon is therefore of paramount importance.PurposesThe objective of this study is to investigate the potential mechanism of action between impaired autophagic flux and increased vulnerability in diabetic myocardium.

title: Plant-derived nanovesicles from Ginkgo biloba seeds mitigate LPS-induced endothelial dysfunction and promote vascular homeostasis
creator: Maneea Moubarak, Emese Szilágyi-Tolnai, Ani Barbulova, Immacolata Fiume, Ildikó Kovács-Forgács, Judit Homoki, Georgina Pesti-Asbóth, Endre Szilágyi, Ramila Mammadova, Matic Kisovec, Marjetka Podobnik, Dávid Papp, Gitta Schlosser, Judit Remenyik, Gabriella Pocsfalvi
description: BackgroundEndothelial dysfunction is increasingly recognized as an early and central event in the onset of cardiovascular and neurodegenerative diseases. Ginkgo biloba extracts are known for their vascular-protective properties, including enhancement of endothelial function, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity, nitric oxide preservation, and modulation of platelet aggregation.

title: Novel tumor-associated macrophage populations and subpopulations by single cell RNA sequencing
creator: Juanjuan Wang, Ningning Zhu, Xiaomin Su, Yunhuan Gao, Rongcun Yang
description: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are present in almost all solid tumor tissues. 16They play critical roles in immune regulation, tumor angiogenesis, tumor stem cell activation, tumor invasion and metastasis, and resistance to therapy. However, it is unclear how TAMs perform these functions.

title: SIK2 antagonizes postinfarction cardiac repair by driving macrophage proinflammatory and impairing efferocytosis
creator: Wu-Wei Rong, Zi-Qi Xu, Shuai Shao, Qian-Wan Deng, Meng-Yao Li, Jin-Qiu Wei, Yi-Hang Yang, Jia-Jia Zhao, Wen-Hui Zhai, Zhi-Wen Shang, Zhi Zhang, Wen-Yi Yang, Shao-Wen Liu, Ping-Jin Gao, Xiao-Dong Li, Ji-Guang Wang
description: Macrophages play a key role in cardiac injury and repair after myocardial infarction (MI). Salt-inducible kinase 2 (SIK2), a member of the adenosine monophosphate–activated protein kinase family, is notably up-regulated in monocytes/macrophages of patients with MI and animal models. In this study, we investigated the role of SIK2 in macrophage-mediated inflammation and efferocytosis following MI.

title: Epidemiology of neonatal disorders attributable to low birthweight-global burden of disease research, 1990–2021
creator: Qi Zhang, Lan Luo, Lai-lai Yan, Jing Guo, Hui-jun Wu, Zi-wei Zhang, Yu-hua Zhu, Rui Qiao
description: BackgroundTo evaluate global, regional, and national trends in the burden of neonatal diseases attributable to LBW, as well as associated health inequalities, from 1990 to 2021.MethodsUsing data from the Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD2021), we analyzed deaths and DALYs due to LBW-attributable neonatal diseases. Data were stratified by gender, geographic region, epidemiological characteristics, and SDI levels.

title: Novel BPI3Vc-vectored surface displayed fusion and hemagglutinin-neuraminidase antigens elicit broadly neutralizing antibodies in cattle
creator: Huldah Sang, Tae Kim, Rakshith Kumar, Jayden McCall, Aloysius Abraham, Tsvetoslav Koynarski, Michelle Zajac, Karim W. Abdelsalam, Daniela Hernandez Muguiro, Katherine Bauer, Brandon L. Plattner, Waithaka Mwangi
description: Bovine parainfluenza-3 virus (BPI3V) contributes to Bovine Respiratory Disease Complex, causing severe pneumonia and death in cattle, leading to economic losses. Existing BPI3V commercial vaccines, based on genotype A strains, confer protection against some, but not all, genotype A strains and induce low neutralizing antibody titers against genotypes B and C.

title: Sustained posterior negativity (SPN) elicited by brief (20 ms) symmetrical stimuli
creator: Giulio Contemori, Marianna Musa, Deniz Demirkapi, Martina Passaggi, Carolina Maria Oletto, Luca Battaglini, Marco Bertamini
description: IntroductionMirror symmetry is detected rapidly, yet it remains unresolved whether its canonical neural signature—the Sustained Posterior Negativity (SPN)—requires extended viewing. We therefore asked whether symmetry-selective activity can be generated under highly constrained temporal conditions that limit both prolonged processing and premotor preparation.

title: MATRIX: Mental heAlth diagnostics Through Real time Intelligent unified X-AI attribution reasoning
creator: Sweety Ramnani, Kaushik Roy, Amit Sheth
description: Escalating prevalence of mental health issues worldwide has created an unprecedented demand for mental healthcare services, yet the shortage of qualified practitioners limits accessibility for countless individuals in need. AI has emerged as a potential solution to support mental health professionals, offering assistance that goes beyond simple diagnostic aid.

title: Associations of economic vulnerability and food insecurity with the Planetary Health Diet in children: PASE study (Brazil)
creator: Érica Priulli, Mariana de Santis Filgueiras, Dayane de Castro Morais, Bruna Clemente Cota, Juliana Farias de Novaes
description: Background/objectivesThis study investigated the associations of economic vulnerability and food insecurity (FI) with the Planetary Health Diet (PHD).MethodsThis cross-sectional study included 378 children aged 8 to 9 years from Viçosa, Minas Gerais, Brazil. Food consumption was assessed using 24-h dietary recalls, and adherence to the PHD was measured using the Planetary Health Diet Index (PHDI).

title: A data-driven AI framework for personalized diagnosis, prognosis, and therapeutic optimization in chronic disease management using multimodal big data analytics
creator: Yu Zhang, Zhujin Song, Qi Cai
description: IntroductionThe transformation of chronic disease management is increasingly driven by the integration of AI and multimodal data analytics, enabling precise, individualized, and scalable healthcare interventions. Despite the growing availability of longitudinal and heterogeneous health data, conventional methods are constrained in their ability to model the complex, patient-specific dynamics inherent to chronic conditions.

title: Ultrafast visual detection of Streptococcus suis via HtpsC‐targeted LAMP–CRISPR–Cas12a coupled with lateral flow immunochromatography
creator: Liu‐xin Li, Miao Xin, Xiao‐wen Cui, Shi‐yin Yu, Fei Meng, Min Cao, Xiao‐hui Xiong, Yi‐chen Lu
description: This study describes a rapid, visual detection platform for Streptococcus suis, a significant zoonotic pathogen, by integrating loop‐mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) with CRISPR–Cas12a and a lateral flow immunochromatographic strip (LFIA) readout. Targeting the conserved HtpsC gene, specific LAMP primers and a PAM‐compliant CrRNA were designed.

title: Prevalence and antimicrobial susceptibility profile of bacteria isolated from the hands of housemaids in Jimma City, Ethiopia
creator: Tadele Shiwito Ango, Negalgn Byadgie Gelaw, Girma Mamo Zegene, Tizita Teshome, Tesfalem Getahun
description: IntroductionBacterial pathogens continue to be a major cause of foodborne gastroenteritis in humans and remain a public health problem. Housemaids operating inside a kitchen could be the source of infection and may transmit disease-inflicting pathogens through contaminated hands.ObjectiveThis study aimed to assess the prevalence and antimicrobial susceptibility profile of bacteria isolated from the hands of housemaids in Jimma City, Ethiopia.

title: Mechanoadaptive nanowire viscoplastic composites with strain-enhanced conductivity for reprocessable bioelectronic interfaces
creator: Ran Huo, Shengyun Huang, Dixiang Gong, Xin Zhou, Heng Zhu, Pengyun Zhang, Hideaki Okuyama, Guangyu Bao, Xuan Li, Aram Bahmani, Lisa Martignetti, Zixin Zhang, Hongyu Hou, Changhong Cao, Yixun Cheng, Wei Gao, Dongling Ma, Nicole Y. K. Li-Jessen, Jianyu Li
description: Bioelectronic interfaces must mechanically conform and adapt to biological tissues while maintaining stable electrical performance during motion and deformation. Existing soft conductors, however, often couple mechanical strain to electrical resistance, accumulate interfacial stress, and hinder reprocessing. Here, we report nanowire viscoplastic composites that combine silver nanowires with a dynamically crosslinked, short-chain polyborosiloxane matrix to produce emergent electromechanical behavior.

title: Cardioprotective and hypotensive mechanistic insights of hydroethanolic extract of Cucumis melo L. kernels in isoprenaline-induced cardiotoxicity based on metabolomics and in silico electrophysiological models
creator: Muqeet Wahid, Fatima Saqib, Ghulam Abbas, Shahid Shah, Abdulrahman Alshammari, Thamer H. Albekairi, Anam Ali, Muhammad Khurm, Mohammad S. Mubarak
description: Background: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) continue to threaten health worldwide, and account for a significant portion of deaths and illnesses. In both developing and industrialized nations, they challenge their health systems. There are several traditional uses of Cucurbitaceae seeds in Pakistan, India, Iran, and China, including treating cardiovascular, neurological, and urogenital diseases.

title: Species-specific roles of the Notch ligands, receptors, and targets orchestrating the signaling landscape of the segmentation clock
creator: Pranav S. Ramesh, Li-Fang Chu
description: Somitogenesis is a hallmark feature of all vertebrates and some invertebrate species that involves the periodic formation of block-like structures called somites. Somites are transient embryonic segments that eventually establish the entire vertebral column. A highly conserved molecular oscillator called the segmentation clock underlies this periodic event and the pace of this clock regulates the pace of somite formation.

title: Phosphosulindac (OXT-328) prevents and reverses chemotherapy induced peripheral neuropathy in mice
creator: Aryah Basu, Jennifer Y. Yang, Vasiliki E. Tsirukis, Andrew Loiacono, Gina Koch, Ishan A. Khwaja, Mahila Krishnamurthy, Nicholas Fazio, Emily White, Aayushi Jha, Shrila Shah, Cameron Takmil, Deniz Bagdas, Aylin Demirer, Adam Master, Ernest Natke, Robert Honkanen, Liqun Huang, Basil Rigas
description: BackgroundChemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN), a side effect of chemotherapy, is particularly difficult to treat. We explored whether phosphosulindac (PS), a modified NSAID, could treat CIPN.MethodsCIPN was induced in male C57BL/6 J mice by paclitaxel, vincristine or oxaliplatin. Mechanical allodynia was measured with the von Frey test and cold allodynia with the acetone test.

title: Promoting continuous rehabilitation with AI-based motion capture and biomechanical analysis: objective feedback as a catalyst
creator: Kotaro Matsuura, Akiko Matsuura, Miwa Izaki, Shigekazu Ishihara, Keiko Ishihara, Kosuke Morinaga, Yuichi Kurita
description: IntroductionExercise therapy is effective for various diseases, but one of the problems in rehabilitation is “continuity” and preventing quitting. This study assumes that objectively tracking changes in motor skills and providing feedback may contribute to the continuity of rehabilitation. Upper limb joint moments were estimated by our program using coordinates obtained through AI-based markerless motion capture.

title: An integrated in vitro approach on the enzymatic and antioxidant mechanisms of four commercially available essential oils (Copaifera officinalis, Gaultheria fragrantissima, Helichrysum italicum, and Syzygium aromaticum) traditionally used topically for their anti-inflammatory effects
creator: Pilar Cebollada, Nelson G. M. Gomes, Paula B. Andrade, Víctor López
description: Introduction: Despite the increasing number of essential oils being reported on their potential therapeutic effects, some remain relatively unknown on their biological properties. That is the case of the essential oils obtained from copaiba (Copaifera officinalis L.), wintergreen (Gaultheria fragrantissima Wall.), everlasting (Helichrysum italicum (Roth) G.Don) and clove (Syzygium aromaticum (L.) Merr. & L.M.

title: Evaluation of 19 years of international external proficiency testing for high-resolution HLA typing
creator: C. E. M. Voorter, L. Groeneveld, S. Heidt, L. Wieten
description: The international high-resolution external proficiency testing (EPT) started in 2004 with high-resolution typing of human leucocyte antigen (HLA) class I (HLA-A,B,C) and HLA class II (HLA-DRB1, DRB345, DQB1, and DPB1) alleles, since possibilities for such an EPT within Europe were limited and all existing EPTs at that time made use of the comparison of HLA typing results without a reference.

title: Predictive power of gait and gait-related cognitive measures in amnestic mild cognitive impairment: a machine learning analysis
creator: Cosimo Tuena, Chiara Pupillo, Chiara Stramba-Badiale, Marco Stramba-Badiale, Giuseppe Riva
description: IntroductionGait disorders and gait-related cognitive tests were recently linked to future Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) dementia diagnosis in amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment (aMCI). This study aimed to evaluate the predictive power of gait disorders and gait-related neuropsychological performances for future AD diagnosis in aMCI through machine learning (ML).MethodsA sample of 253 aMCI (stable, converter) individuals were included.

title: Genomic and transcriptomic analysis of genes involved in exopolysaccharide biosynthesis by Streptococcus thermophilus IMAU20561 grown on different sources of nitrogen
creator: Yuenan Wang, Qingting Peng, Yang Liu, Na Wu, Yanyan He, Xinrui Cui, Tong Dan
description: Exopolysaccharides (EPSs), which are produced by lactic acid bacteria, have been found to improve the texture and functionality of fermented dairy products. In a previous study, four nitrogen sources were identified as affecting the yield, molecular weight and structure of EPSs produced by Streptococcus thermophilus IMAU20561 in M17 medium.

title: Genomic epidemiology and antimicrobial resistance of Morganella clinical isolates between 2016 and 2023
creator: Wentao Zhu, Qian Liu, Jinlv Liu, Yaqi Wang, Hong Shen, Ming Wei, Ji Pu, Li Gu, Jing Yang
description: Morganella morganii is a Gram-negative, opportunistic pathogen that is often associated with nosocomial infections. Here, the genomic characteristics and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) of Morganella clinical isolates between 2016 and 2023 were determined. A total of 218 clinical isolates were mainly identified from urinary tract (48.2%) and respiratory tract (16.5%), with 105 isolates randomly selected for whole genome sequencing.

title: Tough on germs, gentle on hands: a cross-sectional study on hand skin health, skincare and hygiene habit changes among medical students in their clinical years in Dubai, the United Arab Emirates
creator: Zainab Al-Abdullah, Maryam Alabdullah, Fatma Alaghbari, Hamda Alfalasi, Amar Hassan, Aida Joseph Azar, Volha Shpadaruk
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionOccupational hand dermatitis (OHD) has become increasingly prevalent in recent years among healthcare worker populations worldwide. The condition can be so debilitating that it leads to sick leave or even career changes.

title: Entry into long-term care disrupts primary care continuity—but only at entry: a national cohort study of transitional and post-entry continuity in facility- and home-based care in Australia
creator: Johannes Schwabe, Brian W Pulling, Gillian E Caughey, Maria Crotty, Helena Williams, Andrew Kellie, Gillian Harvey, David Roder, Krystal-Lee Nixon, Janet K Sluggett, Monica Cations, Tiffany K Gill, Jyoti Khadka, Megan Corlis, Carolyn Dawkins, Marilyn von Thien, Maria C Inacio
description: BackgroundContinuity of primary care is central to older adults’ health and wellbeing, but entry into long-term care can disrupt established care relationships.ObjectivesThis study aimed to characterize how continuity of care evolves across the transition into long-term care and the post-entry period, comparing facility-based and home-based care, with analyses stratified by metropolitan and non-metropolitan location.

title: Community-engaged clinical governance and machine learning for optimizing tuberculosis management in rural Eastern Cape
creator: Lindiwe Modest Faye, Ntandazo Dlatu, Mojisola Clara Hosu, Wezile Wilson Chitha, Teke Apalata
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global health challenge, particularly in high-burden, resource-limited settings. Community-Engaged Clinical Governance (CE-CG) has emerged as a promising framework for strengthening accountability, adherence, and continuity of care by integrating clinical governance and community participation. This study examined the alignment between CE-CG implementation and TB treatment outcomes in the rural Eastern Cape, South Africa, using patient data from 2018 to 2020.

title: Eye-tracking biomarkers of clinical expertise in ECG interpretation: statistical and machine learning evidence
creator: Eyad Talal Attar
description: IntroductionInterpreting the electrocardiogram (ECG) is a fundamental clinical skill, and mistakes are still prevalent in the workforce, especially among trainees and non-specialist clinicians. Eye-tracking technology has recently become a popular method for investigating visual expertise. However, few studies have integrated visual behavior metrics with machine learning to accurately classify expertise levels.

title: TaRECQ4 contributes to maintain both homologous and homoeologous recombination during wheat meiosis
creator: Jeanne Bazile, Isabelle Nadaud, Pauline Lasserre-Zuber, Jonathan Kitt, Romain De Oliveira, Frédéric Choulet, Pierre Sourdille
description: IntroductionMeiotic recombination (or crossover, CO) is essential for gamete fertility as well as for alleles and genes reshuffling that is at the heart of plant breeding. However, CO remains a limited event, which strongly hampers the rapid production of original and improved cultivars.

title: Study protocol of a double-blind randomized control trial of transcranial direct current stimulation in post-stroke fatigue
creator: Wai Kwong Tang, Hanna Lu, Thomas Wai Hong Leung, Jong S. Kim, Kenneth Nai Kuen Fong
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). RationalePost-stroke fatigue (PSF) is a frequent problem in stroke survivors and often hinders their rehabilitation. PSF is difficult to treat, and pharmacological therapy is often ineffective. Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) can modulate motor, sensory, cognitive and behavioral responses, as it alters neuronal activity by delivering a small amount of current via the scalp to the cortex, resulting in prolonged alterations to brain function.

title: Enjoyment of spinning exercise performed in a group session as compared to an individual session
creator: Katrine Trøstrup Beck, Karoline Sofie Lowater, Jan Rafn, Ernst Albin Hansen
description: IntroductionThe degree of perceived enjoyment of performed physical activity may be a key aspect with relevance for the effort to get people to be physically active. Spinning, or indoor cycling, is a widespread physical activity that can be performed in a group or individually. The effect of the group element on the enjoyment of spinning remains unclear.

title: Contextual adaptation of digital wellbeing interventions for young people: insights from a project in Saudi Arabia
creator: Dahlia Aljuboori, Laura K. Clary, Saud Abdulaziz Alomairah, Michelle Colder Carras, Nazmus Saquib, Juliann Saquib, Fahad Albeyahi, Antonius J. Van Rooij, Anouk Tuijnman, Vincent G. Van der Rijst, Michelle R. Kaufman, Johannes Thrul
description: In today’s world, the internet is seamlessly woven into every facet of our existence. This constant engagement with digital media has generated concerns about the negative effects of digital media use, especially among adolescents. These concerns have led to the development and testing of numerous digital wellbeing interventions that focus on adolescents’ digital media use.

title: Genetic mapping, marker development, and identification of candidate genes for powdery mildew resistance in Malus baccata ‘Jackii’
creator: Matthias Pfeifer, Leonard Kurzweg, Buist Muçaj, Tom Burkhardt, Andreas Peil, Henryk Flachowsky, Ofere Francis Emeriewen, Thomas Wolfgang Wöhner
description: Powdery mildew, caused by Podosphaera leucotricha, is one of the most important fungal diseases in apple cultivation worldwide. Malus baccata ‘Jackii’, however, exhibits resistance to this pathogen, and a previous study demonstrated that this resistance, designated Plbj, co-segregates with an AFLP marker on linkage group 10.

title: Evolutionary Inferences Based on Thoracic Limb Muscles of South American Coati (Nasua nasua): Brachium and Craniolateral Antebrachium
creator: Juan Fernando Vélez García, Roseâmely Angélica de Carvalho Barros, Maria Angelica Miglino
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The South American coati ( Nasua nasua ) is a mammal of the order Carnivora and family Procyonidae, characterized by scansorial locomotion. Accordingly, several anatomical and functional studies examined its thoracic limbs. Nevertheless, the anatomical descriptions and terminology differ among those studies, and none considered the evolutionary derivations of the brachium and antebrachium muscles based on topology, innervation and anatomical variants.

title: Lightweight deep learning for tomato disease detection: trends, challenges, and edge AI perspectives
creator: Harshinisree Gunasekaran, Sujatha Rajkumar, Lincy Kirubhadharsini B.
description: Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) is a globally cultivated horticultural crop, yet its productivity is severely constrained by foliar and insect-vectored diseases that reduce its quality and production. Early and accurate diagnosis of these diseases, along with sustainable biocontrol strategies, is essential for improving crop health and reducing economic losses.

title: Reversal of refractory epilepsy in an adult with GAMT deficiency: A case report and comparative literature review
creator: Wei‐Hung Sung, Hsi Chen, Che‐Wei Hsu, Meng‐Han Tsai
description: ObjectiveGuanidinoacetate methyltransferase (GAMT) deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive creatine biosynthesis disorder. Reports specifically focusing on adult patients remain scarce.MethodsWe report a 52‐year‐old female (the oldest documented case of GAMT deficiency to date) presenting with severe intellectual disability, refractory epilepsy, and adult‐onset disease progression. Whole‐exome sequencing identified novel compound heterozygous GAMT variants (c.265_267del and c.

title: Deep learning reveals ecological decoupling and rate heterogeneity in Hymenoptera wing evolution
creator: Ancheng Peng, Shihan Guan, Laurent Albera, Régine Le Bouquin Jeannès, Huazhong Shu, Mathieu Boderau, André Nel, Bo Wang, Corentin Jouault, Frédéric Legendre
description: Quantifying biomorphological evolution and integrating phenotypic data into large-scale ecological and evolutionary studies are often limited by the scalability, subjectivity, and poor interpretability of existing methods. We introduce HAIKA (Hierarchical Attention-based Interpretable K-dimensional Autoencoder), a self-supervised residual channel-attention autoencoder that extracts continuous morphological representations from unlabeled standardized images and highlights the image regions that contribute to those representations.

title: COVID-19 lateral flow test image classification using deep CNN and StyleGAN2
creator: Vishnu Pannipulath Venugopal, Lakshmi Babu Saheer, Mahdi Maktabdar Oghaz
description: IntroductionArtificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare can enhance clinical workflows and diagnoses, particularly in large-scale operations like COVID-19 mass testing. This study presents a deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for automated COVID-19 RATD image classification.MethodsTo address the absence of a RATD image dataset, we crowdsourced 900 real-world images focusing on positive and negative cases.

title: Re-analysis of the current status of clinical trial registration in China
creator: Shuwen Li, Jianhao Li, Wenjing Zeng, Zhicheng Li, Jietong Zhang, Siying Wang, Nenggui Xu, Zeli Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveTo reanalyze and summarize the current status and deficiencies of clinical trial registration in China, based on an analysis of the situation of clinical trial registration in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR).MethodsA search was conducted in China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Chinese BioMedical Literature Database (CBM), Wangfang Data, VIP Database for Chinese Technical Periodicals (VIP), Web of Science (WoS), PubMed up to December 31, 2023, for literature on the analysis of clinical trial registration based on ChiCTR.

title: Metformin dosage and galectin-3 levels: insights from PCOS patients preparing for IVF
creator: Valentina N. Nikolić, Milan Stefanović, Dejan Mitić, Slavica Sunarić, Vladana Stojiljkovic, Hristina Trajković, Aleksandra Ignjatović, Dragana Stokanović
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study explores the impact of metformin dosage and hyperprolactinemia on galectin-3 levels in women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), providing novel insights into their roles in the metabolic and hormonal management of the condition. A cohort of 53 women, diagnosed using the Rotterdam criteria and undergoing in vitro fertilization (IVF) preparation, was analyzed to determine how these factors influence galectin-3, a biomarker in PCOS.

title: Telenursing on primary family caregivers and children with disabilities: a scoping review
creator: Kaori Nishigaki, Noyuri Yamaji, Naho Adachi, Tomoko Kamei, Kyoko Kobayashi, Shota Kakazu, Yuki Yonekura
description: IntroductionDespite the need for continued support for children with disabilities and their families, COVID-19 has made the support difficult. Telenursing can monitor daily life and support from a remote location, continuously and at a low cost. However, there are few practical reports on its use in children with disabilities.

title: A concise mathematical description of signal transformations across the hippocampal apical CA3 to CA1 dendritic response
creator: Sandra Gattas, Aliza A. Le, Javad Karimi Abadchi, Ben Pruess, Rohit Amba, Yanning Shen, A. Swindlehurst, Michael A. Yassa, Gary Lynch
description: The synapse is the fundamental unit of communication in the nervous system. Determining how information is transferred across the synaptic interface is one of the most complex endeavors in neuroscience, owing to the large number of contributing factors and events.

title: Chronic hypoxia disrupts T regulatory cell phenotype contributing to the emergence of exTreg-TH17 cells
creator: Benjamin J. Lantz, Mika Moriwaki, Olufunmilola M. Oyebamiji, Yan Guo, Laura Gonzalez Bosc
description: The imbalance between pro-inflammatory T helper 17 (TH17) cells and anti-inflammatory regulatory T cells (Tregs) has been implicated in multiple inflammatory and autoimmune conditions, but the effects of chronic hypoxia (CH) on this balance have yet to be explored. CH-exposed mice have an increased prevalence of TH17 cells in the lungs with no change in Tregs.

title: Review of the aetiologies of central nervous system infections in Vietnam
creator: Hannah E. Brindle, Marc Choisy, Robert Christley, Neil French, Michael Griffiths, Pham Quang Thai, H. Rogier van Doorn, Behzad Nadjm
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Central nervous system (CNS) infections are an important cause of morbidity and mortality in Vietnam, with many studies conducted to determine the aetiology. However, the cause remains unknown in a large proportion of cases. Although a systematic review of the aetiologies of CNS infections was conducted in the Mekong region, there are no known published reviews of the studies specifically in Vietnam.

title: Is synthetic data generation effective in maintaining clinical biomarkers? Investigating diffusion models across diverse imaging modalities
creator: Abdullah Hosseini, Ahmed Serag
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionThe integration of recent technologies in medical imaging has become a cornerstone of modern healthcare, facilitating detailed analysis of internal anatomy and pathology. Traditional methods, however, often grapple with data-sharing restrictions due to privacy concerns.

title: Representations of female characters in Bollywood cinema: stereotypes, audience perceptions, and societal impacts
creator: Forhana Choudhury, Swati Sharma
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionThe study aims to examine how audiences perceive the contrasting portrayals of the female lead (heroine) and the item girl in Bollywood films, and to analyse how these binary representations reflect attitudes toward women's roles and identities.

title: Humans experienced abrupt environmental changes at White Sands during the Last Glacial Maximum
creator: Kathleen B. Springer, Jeffrey S. Pigati, Jessica E. Tierney, Jeffrey S. Honke, Gonzalo Jiménez-Moreno, David Bustos, Thomas M. Urban, Daniel Odess, Edward A. Jolie, Alison J. Smith, Abigail J. Hunt, Patrick J. Martinez, Vincent L. Santucci, Sally C. Reynolds, Matthew R. Bennett
description: Expanded excavations at White Sands National Park have unearthed 20 stratigraphic horizons containing in situ human footprints, megafaunal trackways, and linear features created by travois. Advances in radiocarbon dating of conifer pollen, combined with ages of aquatic seeds, refines the chronology of the footprint-bearing sequence to between 23.5 and 21.7 thousand years ago (ka).

title: Moderate regular physical exercise can help in alleviating the systemic impact of schistosomiasis infection on brain cognitive function
creator: Inssaf Berkiks, Nada Abdel Aziz, Blessing Moses, Tiroyaone Brombacher, Frank Brombacher
description: One of the major consequences of schistosomiasis is its impact on brain function, and despite its severity, the underlying mechanism(s) remain inadequately understood, highlighting a knowledge gap in the disease. The symptoms can vary from headaches to profound cognitive impairment. Besides, the potential influence of physical exercise in mitigating cognitive deficits has received little attention.

title: Hu-lu-su-pian ameliorates hepatic steatosis by regulating CIDEA expression in AKT-driven MASLD mice
creator: Rumeng Ren, Qi Wang, Dongjie Deng, Aoao Guo, Xin Chen, Yan Meng, Ying Fang, Guohua Zheng, Zhong Xu, Man Li, Junjie Hu
description: IntroductionHu-lu-su-pian (HLSP) is an oral tablet derived from the active compounds of Cucumis melo L., a traditional Chinese medicine. This contemporary formulation is frequently employed in clinical settings for the management of liver ailments. However, the molecular mechanism by which HLSP affects metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remains unclear.

title: Case report: Novel ACTN4 variant of uncertain significance in a pediatric case of steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome requesting kidney transplantation
creator: Ignacio Alarcón, Carolina Peralta, Francisco Cammarata-Scalisi, Maykol Araya Castillo, Francisco Cano, Angélica Rojo, María Luisa Ceballos, Paola Krall
description: BackgroundSteroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS) is a rare kidney disease commonly characterized histopathologically by focal and segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) or minimal change disease. One-third of SRNS-FSGS cases are attributed to a genetic cause ultimately leading to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) during childhood or adulthood.

title: Genome-wide investigation of ABCB, PIN, and AUX/LAX gene families and their involvement in the formation of leaf protrusions in Sesamum indicum
creator: Yanli Li, Yujia Ma, Huihui Gong, Xinxiao Cui, Xin Wang, Yuling Dong, Ying Chen, Junsheng Zhao
description: Sesamum indicum, a highly esteemed oil crop, has exhibited remarkable value and potential in diverse areas encompassing the economy, food industry, and health. We have observed that there are small protrusions on the leaves of the indehiscent capsule material G1358. No obvious difference was detected on overall auxin content between the leaves of G1358 and LZ1 from metabolomic analysis.

title: The curvilinear relationship between Framingham Steatosis Index and depression: insights from a nationwide study
creator: Chunqi Jiang, Bo Wang, Ning Wang, Jun Wang, Yinuo Qu, Guang Zhao, Xin Zhang
description: BackgroundThe Framingham Steatosis Index (FSI) serves as a diagnostic metric for fatty liver. While research has established a link between depression and fatty liver, the association with the Framingham Steatosis Index (FSI) remains undocumented. The aim of this study is to explore the potential correlation between FSI and depression, addressing this research void.

title: Photomapping electrically coupled networks of the mature thalamus and cortex
creator: Mitchell J. Vaughn, David S. Uygun, Radhika Basheer, Kevin J. Bender, Julie S. Haas
description: Electrical synapses are expressed ubiquitously across the brain and are crucial components of active neural circuitry and connectomes. Identification of coupled networks in living tissue is limited by technical demands of multiplexed recordings, and no dyes, fluorescent reporters, or genetic labels can now fill the gap.

title: Effects of probiotic supplementation on growth and meat quality of Simmental bulls
creator: Yongqing Liu, Gaifang Wang, Rui Wang, Ying He, Xia Zhang, Caiping Feng
description: Probiotics are well established to enhance animal immunity and gastrointestinal health, while also improving meat tenderness and antioxidant status. This study evaluated the effects of dietary probiotic supplementation on growth and meat quality of Simmental bulls. Forty Simmental bulls were randomly assigned by body weight to one of four groups, receiving a basal diet supplemented with probiotics at 0, 0.

title: Conducting and interpreting disproportionality analyses derived from spontaneous reporting systems
creator: Paola Maria Cutroneo, Daniele Sartori, Marco Tuccori, Salvatore Crisafulli, Vera Battini, Carla Carnovale, Concetta Rafaniello, Annalisa Capuano, Elisabetta Poluzzi, Ugo Moretti, Emanuel Raschi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Spontaneous reporting systems remain pivotal for post-marketing surveillance and disproportionality analysis (DA) represents a recognized approach for early signal detection. Although DAs cannot be used per se as a standalone approach to assess a drug-related risk and cannot replace clinical judgment in the individual patient, their role remain irreplaceable for rapid detection of rare and unpredictable adverse drug reactions with strong drug-attributable component (e.g., designated medical events), especially when developed by a multidisciplinary team and combined with a careful case-by-case analysis (individual

title: Membrane vesicles in Acidithiobacillia class extreme acidophiles: influence on collective behaviors of ‘Fervidacidithiobacillus caldus’
creator: Stefano Rossoni, Simón Beard, María Ignacia Segura-Bidermann, Juan Duarte-Ramírez, Francisco Kirhman Osorio, Manuel Varas-Godoy, Patricio Martínez-Bellange, Mario Vera, Raquel Quatrini, Matías Castro
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Membrane vesicles (MVs) are envelope-derived extracellular sacs that perform a broad diversity of physiological functions in bacteria. While considerably studied in pathogenic microorganisms, the roles, relevance, and biotechnological potential of MVs from environmental bacteria are less well established. Acidithiobacillaceae family bacteria are active players in the sulfur and iron biogeochemical cycles in extremely acidic environments and drivers of the leaching of mineral ores contributing to acid rock/mine drainage (ARD/AMD) and industrial bioleaching.

title: 3D printed magnesium silicate/β-tricalcium phosphate scaffolds promote coupled osteogenesis and angiogenesis
creator: Lulu Wang, Mingkui Shen, Zhongxin Tang, Jun Tan, Kuankuan Li, Haijun Ma
description: Fabricating bone tissue engineering substitutes with functional activity remains a challenge for bone defect repair requiring coordinated coupling between osteogenesis and angiogenesis. In this research, we evaluated and analyzed magnesium silicate/β-Tricalcium phosphate (MS/β-TCP) scaffold on angiogenesis and bone regeneration in vitro and in vivo, and the mechanism of its action were described.

title: Case report: POEMS syndrome masquerades as diabetic foot
creator: Guang-Xin Zhou, Li Xiao, Yong-Min Bi, Fen Yang, Cai-Zhe Yang, Da Zhang
description: We present the case of a 54-year-old woman with reasonable blood sugar control who presented with a diabetic foot combined with severe peripheral neuropathy and vascular disease. Lower limb muscle weakness, muscle atrophy, skin pigmentation, and emaciation were also observed.

title: Comprehensive identification of microbial and metabolomic factors impacting ICC recurrence
creator: Yuan Dang, Shaohua Xu, Jingyun Huang, Xing Peng, Yong Yang, Yingchao Wang, Yanan Yan, Fengle Jiang, Jianmin Wang, Jingfeng Liu
description: IntroductionIntrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) originates from intrahepatic bile duct epithelial cells and its global incidence is rising. Surgery remains the primary treatment, but postoperative recurrence rates remain high.MethodsWe analyzed ICC patients' gut microbiota at four stages (preoperative, 7 days postoperative, 1 month postoperative, and during recurrence) using 16S rRNA sequencing and their serum metabolome via LC-MS/MS.

title: Pyramid urethral mobilisation hypospadias repair for distal variant: experience with 70 cases
creator: Mircea Andriescu, Olivia Stanciu, Iulia Stoicescu, Laura Balanescu, Radu Balanescu
description: IntroductionChoosing the appropriate surgical procedure for distal hypospadias is challenging due to the numerous techniques currently used. Urethral mobilization is an adjunctive surgical technique that aims to improve the position of the urethral meatus. We present our experience with a technique of urethral advancement in 70 cases of distal hypospadias.

title: SPRIZ (CCDC127) protein conserved in deuterostome animals is a rigid OMM–IMM tether that locally sets mitochondrial IMS volume
creator: Raman Shulinski, Roman Loban, Danny Farhat, Benjamín Cartes-Saavedra, Matthew J. Magda, Pavel Kotchetkov, Victoria Caminiti, Linda David, Yuri I. Wolf, Conor O’Dwyer, Morgan Fullerton, Yan Burelle, Jyh-Yeuan (Eric) Lee, Andrea Raimondi, Eugene V. Koonin, György Hajnóczky, Mary-Ellen Harper, Luca Pel
description: The double-membrane nature of mitochondria generates an intermembrane volume through which ions, reactive oxygen species, and metabolites must flux to reach the matrix or cytosol, but whether this volume is a genetically specified structure remains unknown. We identify SPRIZ (spatial regulator of the intermembrane zone), the product of Ccdc127, a gene conserved across deuterostome animals.

title: Investigating key elements of digital resilience among nursing undergraduates: a qualitative study
creator: Fanfan Li, Qiuping Ma, Chunxiao Yang, Mingyang Zhong
description: ObjectiveTo explore key elements of digital resilience in nursing undergraduates, providing a foundation for comprehensive assessment and training during medical colleges’ digital transformation.MethodsConducted semi-structured interviews with 20 nursing undergraduates experienced in online learning or digital resource use from March–May 2024, utilizing descriptive qualitative research and directed content analysis.

title: Global conservation additionality hindered by persisting fishing pressure in marine protected areas
creator: Millenne Ohanna, Juliette Jacquemont, Joachim Claudet
description: Marine protected areas (MPAs) are the cornerstone of global marine conservation strategies. Yet, their capacity to achieve conservation gains (i.e., conservation additionality) hinges on the decrease in human threats to biodiversity within their boundary, a feature rarely measured or reported.

title: Impact of depth-of-interaction and spatially-variant point-spread-function model on the performance of ultra-high resolution brain PET
creator: Tianyi Zeng, Yassir Najmaoui, Jiazhen Zhang, Tommaso Volpi, Kathryn Fontaine, Yanis Chemli, Yifan Hu, Jean-Dominique Gallezot, Chen Sun, Yihuan Lu, Georges El Fakhri, Richard E Carson, Thibault Marin
description: Objective. To implement a spatially-variant point spread function (VarPSF) model for the NeuroEXPLORER (NX) brain positron emission tomography (PET) scanner in the open-source Yale Reconstruction Toolkit for PET, and investigate the interplay between depth-of-interaction (DOI) resolution and resolution modeling. Approach. PSF parameters were estimated from simulated and physically measured point sources.

title: Avian cecal microbiome response and resilience to Newcastle disease are dictated by breed background
creator: Aqsa Ameer, Farrukh Saleem, Ciara Keating, Farhan Afzal, Hamid Irshad, Khurshid Ahmed, Sadia Sattar, Umer Zeeshan Ijaz, Sundus Javed
description: A wide range of viral infections threaten the long-term sustainability of poultry production. Newcastle disease (ND), caused by Newcastle disease virus (NDV), is endemic in most Asian countries, including Pakistan, causing 50%–100% mortality in young and mature chickens. Some local chicken breeds show resistance to certain diseases and have greater survival probability.

title: UniProt data pruning and the growing invisibility of the dark proteome
creator: Ali Al-Fatlawi, Michael Schroeder
description: The protein resource UniProtKB has undergone a major, multi-stage reorganization of its protein space, implemented from release 2025_04 through release 2026_02. Analysis of UniProtKB and UniParc records accessed on 20 January 2026 showed that 125.9 million entries were last present in UniProtKB in 2025 and are now represented in UniParc, while ~200.

title: Liquid Chromatography Coupled With High‐Resolution Mass Spectrometry Profiling of Metabolites in Cassia alata Flower Extracts and Their DPPH Free Radical Scavenging Activity
creator: Adonai Yin‐Anaab Kunduzore, Shakira Ibrahim, Auphedeous Yinme Dang‐i, Michael Adu‐Frimpong, Salma Elshamy, Nikolai Kuhnert, James Ziemah
description: Cassia alata flowers remain phytochemically under‐characterized relative to the leaves. However, floral tissues can harbour distinct and, in some species, more abundant phenolic and flavonoid profiles, representing an unexploited source of antioxidant phytochemicals with potential functional‐food and nutraceutical relevance. Also, Cassia alata L.

title: Microbes from ambient-pressure analogues offer insights into possible life in Europa’s high-pressure subsurface ocean
creator: Alvaro del Moral, Dominic Siggs, Michael C. Macey, Mark G. Fox-Powell, Victoria K. Pearson, Karen Olsson-Francis
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Under its thick ice layer, Europa contains a shielded liquid water ocean where habitable conditions may exist. To effectively assess the habitability of this environment and the implications on putative biosignature formation, it is essential to integrate our understanding of the physicochemical conditions of the sub-surface ocean with ground-truth analysis on Earth, using both natural analogue sites and laboratory simulation experiments.

title: Xp21 DNA microdeletion syndrome in a Chinese family: clinical features show retinitis pigmentosa and chronic granuloma
creator: Mengyang Li, Xueqin Hu, Xueli Wu, Na Zhao, Yuanyuan Lian, Meijiao Ma, Huiping Li, Xunlun Sheng
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Xp21 DNA microdeletion syndrome is a very rare disease characterized by retinitis pigmentosa (RP), chronic granulomatous disease (CGD), and McLeod syndrome (MLS). Due to the complex and diverse clinical manifestations, early diagnosis remains a challenge for many physicians.

title: Transitioning of protein substitutes in patients with phenylketonuria: a pilot study
creator: Ozlem Yilmaz Nas, Catherine Ashmore, Sharon Evans, Alex Pinto, Anne Daly, Nurcan Yabanci Ayhan, Anita MacDonald
description: IntroductionIn phenylketonuria (PKU), there is limited information about transitioning between protein substitutes and the influencing factors, particularly in young children. This pilot study assessed the stepwise transition from second to third-stage protein substitutes in children with PKU, aged 3–5 years.MethodsDemographics, child behavior, maternal anxiety, and food neophobia scores were collected at baseline, mid-transition, and final assessment.

title: Domesticated bacterial origin genes regulate homeostasis of the insect gut microbiome and empower adaptation
creator: Zhenjia Zhang, Yubo Zhang, Kun Zhao, Guangyuan Cheng, Zhihao Lu, Dongju Wang, Yiqun Liu, Jianguo Wu, Liying Wang, Lisheng Zhang, Xinhai Ye, Li Yu, Wei Zhang, Yi Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Sap‐sucking insects, represented by the globally distributed leafhoppers, have evolved a wide range of adaptive traits and play multiple ecological roles. However, their successful survival strategies in nature remain poorly understood. To explore the adaptive mechanisms of sap‐sucking insects, we established a research system using three representative leafhopper species from the same family and found that they have acquired multiple cholesterol‐dependent cytolysins (CDCs) derived from gram‐positive bacterial genes.

title: Building a foundation to promote Women’s health research in Dubai. Study protocol for a project to investigate the feasibility of establishing a dedicated Women’s health biobank
creator: William Atiomo, Fadi Mirza, Khawla Al Zarooni, Muna Tahlak, Tom Loney, Asiyah Shafi, Osman Zin Al Abdin, Mahmood Al Mashhadani, Samuel Ho, Arnaud Wattiez, Manal AbdulRahim, Mutairu Ezimokhai
description: Women’s health concerns play a role in several of the UAE's major public health challenges, including cardiovascular disease, injuries, cancer, and respiratory conditions. The UAE's 2024 National Policy for improving Women’s health aims to lower cancer mortality rates to 23.24 per 100,000 females, with translational research projects utilizing bio-registries and biobanks supporting this goal.

title: Biobased Boston Ivy‐Inspired Cryogel Integrating Radiative Cooling and Phase Change Energy Storage for Adaptive Thermal Regulation
creator: Sining Huang, Zhiguo Li, Yang Liu, Chengyu Wang, Yi Lu, Erlantz Lizundia, Siqi Huan
description: Boston ivy is a traditional plant for building heat management through shading and transpiration. Inspired by its “vine‐leaf” system, we design a bionic cryogel that functionalizes daytime cooling and nighttime thermal buffering, promoting sustainable and comfortable housing and living environments. The aligned channels mimic vine tendrils, delivering an ultralow radial thermal conductivity (0.035 W m−1·K−1), high solar reflectance (95.

title: Detection of human papillomavirus (HPV)-specific T cell response in women with low-grade cervical intraepithelial lesion and HPV vaccinated subjects
creator: Paola Zelini, Federica Zavaglio, Mattia Dominoni, Marta Valsecchi, Lucrezia Lo Grasso, Piera d’Angelo, Federica Giardina, Greta Romano, Stefania Paolucci, Daniele Lilleri, Irene Cassaniti, Arsenio Spinillo, Fausto Baldanti, Barbara Gardella
description: BackgroundHuman papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted infection worldwide and HPV-driven cervical cancers remain a major health concern. This study aimed primarily to develop a test for assessing and characterizing HPV-specific T-cell responses, in HPV-vaccinated women and women with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN)1.

title: Task-specific theta enhancement and domain-general alpha/beta suppression as oscillatory signatures of cognitive flexibility
creator: Mareike Hülsemann, Christoph Löffler, Anna-Lena Schubert
description: Cognitive flexibility–the ability to adapt to changing situational or task demands–is a fundamental aspect of human cognition and a potential source of individual differences in higher-order cognitive abilities. To further understand the neural mechanisms underlying this ability, we examined event-related spectral perturbations (ERSP) in three cued switching tasks (parity/magnitude, global/local, number/letter) in a sample of 148 adults.

title: A review of Brucea javanica: metabolites, pharmacology and clinical application
creator: Jing Chen, Dongke Yu, Xinyu Li, Qichuan Deng, Hao Yang, Lu Chen, Lan Bai
description: This review examines advances in the metabolites, pharmacological research, and therapeutic applications of the medicinal fruit of Brucea javanica (L.) Merr. Brucea javanica (BJ) is derived from the fruit of the Brucea javanica (L.) Merr. There are nearly 200 metabolites present in BJ, and due to the diversity of its metabolites, BJ has a wide range of pharmacological effects.

title: The effect of cannabis-derived terpenes on alveolar macrophage function
creator: Patrick M. Greiss, Jacquelyn D. Rich, Geoffrey A. McKay, Dao Nguyen, Mark G. Lefsrud, David H. Eidelman, Carolyn J. Baglole
description: Cannabis sativa (marijuana) is used by millions of people around the world. C. sativa produces hundreds of secondary metabolites including cannabinoids, flavones and terpenes. Terpenes are a broad class of organic compounds that give cannabis and other plants its aroma. Previous studies have demonstrated that terpenes may exert anti-inflammatory properties on immune cells.

title: The long arc of scientists in spaceflight: scientists flying with their experiments
creator: Robert J Ferl
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Recent developments in commercial suborbital spaceflight have expanded opportunities for researchers to fly with their experiments. In an accompanying paper in npj Microgravity, we report results from a researcher-tended experiment aboard Blue Origin New Shepard flight NS-261.

title: Handwriting but not typewriting leads to widespread brain connectivity: a high-density EEG study with implications for the classroom
creator: F. R. (Ruud) Van der Weel, Audrey L. H. Van der Meer
description: As traditional handwriting is progressively being replaced by digital devices, it is essential to investigate the implications for the human brain. Brain electrical activity was recorded in 36 university students as they were handwriting visually presented words using a digital pen and typewriting the words on a keyboard.

title: Radiation-induced glymphatic dysfunction in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a study using diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space
creator: Xingyou Zheng, Jianchun Peng, Qing Zhao, Li Li, Jian-ming Gao, Keyang Zhou, Bei Tan, Lingling Deng, Youming Zhang
